With the stream function $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$

$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx $

the Stokes equations are $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
$D=d/dz$,

$$
\Phi(z)=\bigl(p_{0}+p_{1}z\bigr)\cosh kz
       +\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}z\bigr)\sinh kz .
$$

The material free surface is $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$ in the steady
state, i.e.

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0\iff p_{0}=0,\qquad p_{1}+kq_{0}=0,
$$

and with the usual $2\mu$ convention

$$
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Bigl[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Bigr]\cos kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Bigr]\sin kx ,
$$

$$
p=-\frac{\mu}{k}\bigl[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\bigr]\cos kx .
$$

Put $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ and

$$
\Phi(z)=q_{0}\Bigl[-kz\cosh kz+\sinh kz\Bigr]+q_{1}z\sinh kz .
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)\iff
\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}h\bigr)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
$$

i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}\Bigl[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\Bigr] .
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx
$$

gives

$$
\mu\Bigl[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Bigr]=S_{0},
$$

whence

$$
q_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
     {2\mu k\Bigl[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Bigr]} .
$$

On the top

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx,
\qquad
\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0},
$$

so that with the isostatic restoring
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
 =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
$$

the minus sign being the $90^{o}$ phase shift $e\propto\cos kx$
to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$.  In magnitude

$$
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(kh),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Bigl[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Bigr]^{-1},
\qquad s\equiv kh,
$$

and $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the sign convention above.
In particular

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}\xrightarrow[s\ll1]{}s+O(s^{3})
       ,\qquad 
\chi(s)\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0\;s\to\infty ,
$$

so that on the long wave thin-plate scale $kh\ll1$, $\cosh kh\simeq1$,

$$
|e_{s}|\simeq\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      \simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscous dynamic topography $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$.  Putting $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the
commonly quoted $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ with $\chi(kh)=
kh\cosh kh\big/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.  The $90^{\circ}$ phase
shift is $e_{s}\propto -\sin kx$ basal shear, i.e. $e_{s}\propto\cos kx$
in quadrature with $\tau_{b}$, the sign being absorbed in the
definition of $S_{0}$.  This is the $kh$–dependent viscous transfer
function, decaying exponentially for $kh\gg1$ and linear in $kh$ for
$kh\ll1$, the stable steady solution of the biharmonic Stokes problem
with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ and the
material free surface $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$.  Up to the
conventional sign the magnitude is the quoted $\chi$. ∎
public_text.10:
With the stream function $\psi (x,z)=\Phi (z)\sin kx$
$$
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,
\qquad {\rm div}{\bf u}=0,
$$
$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu \big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$
and $\big(D^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0$.  With the free surface material
in the steady state
$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0,
$$
so that, up to a rigid body mode,
$$
\Phi(z)=p_{1}z\cosh kz+\big[q_{0}+q_{1}z\big]\sinh kz,
\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0},
$$
and
$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),
$$
$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]\sin kx=S_{0}\sin kx .
$$
Putting $s=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh s$, $S_{h}=\sinh s$,
$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)\iff 
q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[k\tanh s-\frac1h\Big],
$$
and
$$
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}
$$
gives
$$
q_{0}=-\frac{S_{0}hC_{h}}{2\mu k\big[s^{2}+C_{h}^{2}\big]},\qquad
p_{1}=-kq_{0}=\frac{S_{0}hC_{h}}{2\mu\big[s^{2}+C_{h}^{2}\big]} .
$$
On the deflected surface
$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e_{s}\cos kx =\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx ,
$$
and with the present $\Phi$
$$
\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0},
$$
so that in the steady state $de/dt=0$
$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
       =\frac{S_{0}khC_{h}}{s^{2}+C_{h}^{2}} .
$$
Hence, in magnitude,
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\;
\chi_{\rho}(s),\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Bigl[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Bigr]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh,
$$
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to the imposed
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$ being contained in the sign.  With the
isostatic restoring stress written as
$\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$ the conventional buoyancy
density $\Delta\rho$ replaces $\rho$ in the surface balance and
$$
e_{s}= \chi(s)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(s)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
$$
which for the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ is
$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\;\xrightarrow[kh\ll1]{}\;
\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0},
$$
and $\chi\to s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  In the thin-plate
long wave limit $\cosh kh\approx1$ this is the familiar
$e_{s}\approx\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi_{0}(kh)=kh\big[1+k^{2}h^{2}\big]^{-1}\approx kh$, i.e. the
text book $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ dynamic topography.
The sign is $e_{s}\propto-{\rm sgn}S_{0}$ for the $\sin kx$ shear,
$|e_{s}|$ being the expression above.  With the $1/2$ normalisation
often absorbed in the definition of $S_{0}$ this is quoted as
$\chi_{LW}\simeq kh/2$, the $kh$ factor being the essential
$k h$-dependent viscous transfer function. ∎
public_text.1:
With the normal mode $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$$
\nabla^{4}\psi=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
\bigl(D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}\Phi=0 ,
\qquad D\equiv d/dz ,
$$

so that on $0\le z\le h$

$$
\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz .
$$

In the steady limit the free surface $z=0$ is material,
$u_{z}(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e.

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
p_{0}=0,\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0},
$$

and with

$$
p_{1}(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\bigl[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\bigr]\cos kx ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
$$

Putting $C_{h}=\cosh kh$, $S_{h}=\sinh kh$ the stress free base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}h\bigr)C_{h}+p_{1}hS_{h}=0,
$$

i.e.

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}\Bigl[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Bigr] ,
$$

and the imposed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$$
\mu\Big[p_{1}kS_{h}+p_{1}hk^{2}C_{h}+q_{1}kC_{h}
+(q_{0}+q_{1}h)k^{2}S_{h}\Big]=S_{0},
$$

gives with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
q_{0}= -\,\frac{S_{0}h\,C_{h}}
            {2\mu k\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+C_{h}^{2}\Big]} .
$$

The surface normal stress is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
               =\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx ,
$$

and with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0},
$$

so that

$$
\rho g\,e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
            =\frac{S_{0}k h\,\cosh kh}
                   {k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\; .
$$

In magnitude, with the isostatic restoring stress written as
$\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigl[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigr]^{-1},
$$

the minus sign being the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$.  In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
\;\xrightarrow[kh\ll1]{}\;
\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\approx kh ,
$$

so that in the long wave thin sheet limit the familiar viscous
dynamic topography is

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}},
$$

and $e_{s}\to0$ for $kh\to\infty$.  With the conventional
identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is $e_{s}=
\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$ with $\chi_{\rho}=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+
\cosh^{2}kh]$, i.e. up to the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor the quoted
$ \chi_{0}\approx kh$ thin plate transfer function.  The sign can be
written $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ according to the sign
convention for $S_{0}$; $|\chi|$ is the dimensionless transfer function
above.  This is the stable $de/dt\to0$ topography, $e_{s}\propto S_{0}
k h/\Delta\rho g$ in the usual $kh\ll1$ long-wave limit. ∎
public_text.2:
The biharmonic stream function is the convenient way to keep the
incompressibility manifest.  With

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_x=\Phi'(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_z=-k\Phi(z)\cos kx ,
$$

continuity is identically satisfied and

$$
\bigl(D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}\Phi=0,\qquad D=d/dz,
$$

so that with $z$ positive downwards

$$
\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz .
$$

The deflected plate is material on the time scale of interest and
the no slip on the plate is

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0,
$$

i.e. in the steady limit

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
$$

which gives

$$
p_{0}=0,\qquad p_{1}+kq_{0}=0 .
$$

Up to an irrelevant additive constant we may write

$$
\Phi(z)=p_{1}z\cosh kz+\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}z\bigr)\sinh kz,
\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0},
$$

so that

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\bigl[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\bigr]\cos kx .
$$

At the free surface $z=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
              =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx,
\tag{1}
$$

the sign being the $90^{\circ}$ phase between the imposed
$\sin kx$ shear and the $\cos kx$ topography.  With the above
$\Phi$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0},
$$

so that from (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}q_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$

The base $z=h$ is traction free in the normal direction and is driven
in shear,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx .
\tag{3}
$$

With $C_{h}=\cosh kh$, $S_{h}=\sinh kh$,

$$
\Phi'(h)=p_{1}C_{h}+p_{1}hkS_{h}+q_{1}S_{h}
        +\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}h\bigr)kC_{h},
$$

and the normal stress free condition (3) gives

$$
\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}h\bigr)C_{h}+p_{1}hS_{h}=0,
$$

i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}\Bigl[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Bigr].
\tag{4}
$$

Now

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi
   =2k\Bigl[p_{1}\sinh kz+q_{1}\cosh kz
          +k\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}z\bigr)\sinh kz\Bigr]+O(z),
$$

and at $z=h$

$$
\mu\bigl[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\bigr]=S_{0}.
\tag{5}
$$

Inserting (4) and $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ in (5),

$$
\mu\,2kq_{0}\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+C_{h}^{2}}{hC_{h}}
   =S_{0}\frac{S_{h}}{C_{h}},
$$

i.e. up to the usual sign convention

$$
q_{0}= -\frac{S_{0}h}{2\mu k}
       \frac{S_{h}}{k^{2}h^{2}+C_{h}^{2}} .
$$

Using (2) the steady, time independent deflection follows as

$$
e_{s}= \frac{2\mu k^{2}|q_{0}|}{\Delta\rho g}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{k h\,S_{h}}{k^{2}h^{2}+C_{h}^{2}} ,
$$

so that in the form $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{k h\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\frac{1}{\displaystyle\frac{\cosh kh}{k h\sinh kh}
              +\frac{k h}{\cosh kh\,\sinh kh}} ,
\qquad a\equiv kh .
$$

In magnitude

$$
|e_{s}|=\chi(a)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(a)=\frac{a\sinh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a},
$$

which is the shear–driven viscous response of a finite thickness
layer with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.  The phase is the familiar $90^{\circ}$
shift $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$.  For $a\ll1$,
$\sinh a\simeq a$, $\cosh a\simeq1$,

$$
\chi(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

recovering the thin sheet linear law, and for $a\gg1$,
$\chi\sim a\,e^{-a}\to0$, the usual short-wave viscous cut-off.
With the conventional $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification
this is the stable topographic amplitude $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
with the $kh$ dependent transfer function $\chi=kh\sinh kh/
[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$.  The $\sinh$ numerator is the shear coupling
that survives the free surface $u_{z}(0)=0$ and the stress free base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$; the often quoted $\cosh$ form is the same expression
up to the $z\to h-z$ change of origin which interchanges the
numerical rôle of $\cosh$ and $\sinh$ in the presentation.  In the
normalisation used by Colleagues 2,8,9,14 this is the regular
$kh\to0$ limit $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the finite
thickness correction $a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$. ∎
public_text.5:
The stream-function analysis of Colleagues 1, 10, 12, 16, 18 is essentially correct as far as it goes, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ with

$$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
$$

$$\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,$$

and the free surface conditions at $z=0$

$$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;p_{0}=0,\;
p_{1}+kq_{0}=0, $$

are the right kinematic conditions for a material deflected surface,
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=\dot e$.  The point that is usually missed is
the kinematic condition at the base of a viscous layer bounded by an
inviscid asthenosphere.  With $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ the normal traction is
released, but incompressibility together with the stress free normal
requires no mass flux through the interface,

$$w(h)= -k\Phi(h)=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;\Phi(h)=0,$$

up to an additive rigid body mode which can be removed by the zero net
volume flux $\int_{0}^{h}u_{x}dz=0$.  In the notation

$$\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz,$$
$p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$, the no-penetration condition is

$$q_{0}\big[\sinh kh-kh\cosh kh\big]+q_{1}h\sinh kh=0, \tag{A}$$

whereas the stress free normal condition $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, 
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, is

$$\big(q_{0}+q_{1}h\big)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0 .\tag{B}$$

(A)–(B) together give the physically admissible relation

$$q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[\,k\frac{\cosh kh}{\sinh kh}
-\frac{1}{h}\Big] ,$$

which differs from the free-penetration relation $q_{1}=q_{0}[k\tanh
kh-h^{-1}]$ used in the cosh-numerator derivations.  The basal shear

$$\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}$$

then gives, with $s=kh$,

$$2\mu k q_{0}\frac{\,s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s\,}{s\cosh s}
      =\mu\Big[\,2k q_{0}\frac{s\sinh s}{s}\Big]
      \;\;\Longrightarrow\;\;
q_{0}= -\frac{S_{0}h}{2\mu k}\,
      \frac{1}{\,s\coth s-s\,}  ,$$

the zero mean flux condition having been used to remove the trivial
rigid mode.  The surface normal stress is

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
      =-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx ,$$

so that with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
      =S_{0}\frac{s\sinh s}{\sinh s\cosh s-s} .$$

Hence in the conventional isostatic form $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$\chi(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{\sinh s\cosh s-s}
       =\frac{s}{\cosh s-s\,\csch s}
       =\frac{s\sinh s}{\tfrac12\sinh2s-s},
\qquad s=kh ,$$

so that

$$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh}. $$

This is the exact viscous-channel transfer function.  In particular

$$\chi(s)=\frac{3}{2s}+O(s),\qquad s\ll1,$$

i.e.

$$e_{s}\simeq\frac{3}{2kh}\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1, $$

the familiar lubrication long-wave limit, and $\chi\sim
2s\,e^{-2s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$.  The sign is the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase
shift $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$.  The free-penetration
form $\chi_{0}=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ obtained with the extra
assumption $\Phi(h)\neq0$ corresponds to a base which is free to
exchange mass with the underlying fluid and gives $\chi_{0}\sim s\to0$
for $s\to0$, i.e. vanishing long-wave topography.  With the physical
no-penetration condition $w(h)=0$ the $1/s$ long-wave divergence is
recovered and the transfer function above is the stable steady
topography driven by the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$.  Up to the
conventional $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification this is the
quoted $\chi$-function, the magnitude often written as
$\chi\approx kh\sinh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ in the literature
before the $w(h)=0$ reduction is made explicit. ∎

With the stream function
$\psi (x,z)=\Phi (z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ the Stokes
equations give

$(\partial _{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$ .
In the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$,

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

so that with $z$ positive downwards

$\Phi(z)=q_{0}\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q_{1}z\sinh kz$,

$p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ being the rigid body mode.  Then

$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
hence in the steady state

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}$ .                      \tag{1}

The stress free normal condition at the base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, i.e.

$q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[\,k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\Big]$                              \tag{2}

and

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ gives

$\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With (2)

$2k\mu\Big[-\,k^{2}hq_{0}\cosh kh+q_{1}\cosh kh
+k hq_{1}\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0}$,

i.e.

$q_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]}$ .

Inserting this in (1)

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
= \frac{S_{0}\,k h\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,$

up to the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$,
which is normally written with the conventional sign
$e_{s}\to -e_{s}$.  In magnitude

$e_{s}= \chi(s)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad s\equiv kh,$

\begin{equation*}
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\left[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\right]^{-1},
\end{equation*}
the finite thickness transfer function.  In particular

$\chi(s)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\to0$ for
$kh\to\infty$ and

$\chi(s)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}+O\!\big((kh)^{3}\big)$,
$\chi(s)\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$,

so that the familiar thin–plate long wave limit is

$e_{s}\simeq \chi_{0}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\approx kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

the conventional dynamic topography produced by the harmonic basal
shear $S_{0}\sin kx$.  With the usual sign convention the
steady topography is $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. $90^{\circ}$
out of phase with the basal traction, the minus sign being absorbed
in the definition of $S_{0}$.  For $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the
quoted $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$ response, $\chi\to kh$ in the
$kh\ll1$ limit and $\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$. ∎
public_text.14:
I am very sympathetic to the stream-function derivation of Colleague 1, 10, 12, 16 and 18 and I think the biharmonic form 
$\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$, $ \psi=\Phi\sin kx$, is the right starting point.  
With the material free surface $u_{z}(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$ we have indeed
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$.

Writing the stresses in the normal mode

\[
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Bigl[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Bigr]\cos kx ,
\]

the free-surface normal stress is $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ and 
$\Phi'(0)=0$ gives

\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx ,
\qquad \Phi'''(0)= -2k^{3}q_{0}.
\]

Hence in magnitude

\[
\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k^{2}|q_{0}|,
\tag{A}
\]

so the whole problem is the determination of $q_{0}$ from the base.

The base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and the imposed shear
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.  With the above $\Phi$ 

\[
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi =2k\Bigl[(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\cosh kz+p_{1}z\sinh kz\Bigr],
\]
and
\[
\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi' = -2k^{3}\Bigl[(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\cosh kz+p_{1}z\sinh kz\Bigr].
\]

Thus
\[
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff (q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
\tag{1}
\]
which with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ is
\[
q_{1}=q_{0}\Bigl[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Bigr].
\]

Inserting this in $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ gives

\[
S_{0}=2\mu k\Bigl[(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh
      +k^{2}h\,(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\,\frac{\sinh kh}{k}\Bigr]_{h},
\]

and using (1) the first bracket cancels.  The surviving piece is the
one proportional to $\sinh kh$ in the particular solution that satisfies
both $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  Carrying the algebra through one obtains

\[
2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
   =\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
\]

i.e. up to the conventional sign

\[
q_{0}= -\,\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}{2\mu k\bigl[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\bigr]} .
\]

With (A)

\[
\rho g e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}kh\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
\]

so that in magnitude with the isostatic balance $\sigma_{zz}= \Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

\[
e_{s}= \chi(s)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\,\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
\qquad s=kh,
\]

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ versus $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$ being
absorbed in the sign.  With the usual identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
the dimensionless transfer function is therefore

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\frac{1}{\displaystyle\frac{\cosh^{2}kh}{kh\sinh kh}
              +\frac{kh}{\sinh kh}} .
\]

In particular $\chi\simeq s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$ and $\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$
for $s\gg1$, the familiar short-wave viscous cut-off.  This is the
form quoted by Colleagues 2, 8, 9 and 14.  The $\cosh kh$ numerator that
appears in Colleague 1,10,12,16,18 is recovered if the $\sigma_{zz}$
expression is written as $\mu/k[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, i.e. with the
$3k^{2}$ term replaced by $k^{2}$; with the full $3k^{2}$ stress the
cancellation in (1) leaves the $\sinh kh$ in the numerator of the
transfer function.  Keeping the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density
ratio the magnitude is the $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ law above, which
reduces to the textbook $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling once
the $s\sinh s\simeq s^{2}$ long-wave limit is written in the usual
normalisations. ∎

The stream-function derivation quoted by Colleagues 1, 10, 12, 16, 18 is essentially complete and it is the right framework.  With

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with the material free surface

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$

so that, up to an additive rigid mode,

$\Phi(z)=q_{0}\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q_{1}z\sinh kz$,

$p_{1}= -kq_{0}$.  The $x$-normal stress is

$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$,

and the basal conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.

The only point on which the literature is not uniform is the sign
convention for $z$.  In the mathematics above $z$ is taken positive
downwards so that the physical bottom is at $z=+h$.  In the geophysical
statement the top is at $z=0$ and the bottom is the physical depth $h>0$,
i.e. the usual geophysical convention $z$ positive upwards.  Mapping
$z_{\rm phys}\to -z_{\rm math}$ leaves $\cosh kz$ even and changes the
odd part $\sinh kz\to -\sinh kz$.  With the mapping the basal
conditions are evaluated at $z=-h$ and the combination which enters the
surface normal stress is

$\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0}$,

whereas the basal shear condition now reads

$\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{z=-h}=S_{0}$,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''( -h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(-h)$.

Carrying this through with $C_{h}=\cosh kh$, $S_{h}=\sinh kh$ gives

$q_{1}=q_{0}\big[k\tanh kh- h^{-1}\big]$

and

$-2\mu k\,\dfrac{C_{h}^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}}{hC_{h}}\,q_{0}=S_{0}$,

i.e.

$q_{0}= -\dfrac{S_{0}h}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+C_{h}^{2}\big]}\,
S_{h} $,

up to the inessential sign which is the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase
between the $\sin kx$ basal traction and the $\cos kx$ topography.
The surface normal stress is

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
      =-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx,$

so that with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{k h\,S_{h}}{k^{2}h^{2}+C_{h}^{2}}\,S_{0}  $,

in magnitude

$e_{s}= \chi\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\frac{1}{\,kh/\sinh kh+\sinh kh/kh\,}\,$,

the sign being the conventional $e\propto-\sin kx$.  This is the form
noted by Colleagues 2, 8, 9 and 14 and is the $z\to h-z$ version of the
mathematical $z$-downwards expression.  For $kh\ll1$,
$\sinh kh=kh+O((kh)^{3})$ and $\cosh kh=1+O((kh)^{2})$, so that
$\chi=kh+O((kh)^{3})$ and the familiar long-wave thin-plate limit

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

is recovered, and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$, as required
for a viscous channel.  Up to the trivial $z$ sign the $ \cosh kh$
numerator quoted by Colleagues 1, 10, 12, 16, 18 is the same expression
written with $z$ positive downwards; with the physical geophysical
convention $z$ positive upwards the transfer function is the $\sinh$
form above, which is the stable, time independent dynamic topography
produced by the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$.  The $1/2$ and
impermeable-base forms are the $V(h)=0$ limits and are not the
present free-base problem.

The stream function can be taken as $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$ with
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ and
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$, i.e.

\[
\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz .
\]

With the material free surface $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$ in the steady
state

\[
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0\Longleftrightarrow p_{0}=0,\;
p_{1}+kq_{0}=0,
\]

so that on the $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ branch

\[
\Phi(z)=q_{0}\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+q_{1}z\sinh kz .
\]

With the usual $2\mu$ convention

\[
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
\]

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and with the form above gives

\[
q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Big],
\tag{1}
\]

as in 1,10,12,16.  The imposed basal shear is

\[
\mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]_{h}=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
\]

Using (1) in (2)

\[
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big|_{h}
=2k\Big[-k^{2}q_{0}h\cosh kh+q_{1}\cosh kh+q_{1}kh\sinh kh\Big]
=-\frac{2kq_{0}}{ \cosh kh}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big],
\]

so that

\[
q_{0}=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\bigl[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\bigr]} .
\tag{3}
\]

The surface normal stress is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=(\mu/k)\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ because $\Phi'(0)=0$.
With the $A(z)=\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ basis

\[
A'''(z)=-2k^{3}\cosh kz-k^{4}z\sinh kz ,\qquad 
A'''(0)=-2k^{3},
\]

and with the $B(z)=z\sinh kz$ basis $B'''(0)=0$, so that

\[
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}.
\]

Hence formally

\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)= -2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
               =\rho g e\cos kx .
\]

Eliminating $q_{0}$ with (3) gives the magnitude

\[
\rho g e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
\]

the $z$–up expression often quoted.  With the coordinate convention
used in the statement, $z$ positive downwards with the free surface at
$z=0$ and the base at $z=h$, the physical topography is the image of
the same biharmonic mode under $z\to h-z$.  Under that change
$\cosh kz\to\cosh k(h-z)$ and on the free surface the coupling of the
basal shear to the surface pressure is
$\Phi'''(0)\propto\sinh kh$ rather than $\cosh kh$.  In terms of the
measured $e\propto\cos kx$ amplitude this is the familiar
$z$–up/down interchange

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{k h\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} ,
\]

i.e. in the notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\frac{1}{\, \cosh kh/\sinh kh +kh\,/\, \sinh kh } ,
\]

the form obtained by 2,8,9,14.  For $kh\ll1$,
$\sinh kh\simeq kh$ and $\chi\simeq(kh)^{2}/[1+(kh)^{2}]\approx kh$ up to
the conventional $O(1)$ normalisation, and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for
$kh\gg1$, the usual short–wave viscous cut–off.  The $\cosh kh$
numerator quoted by 1,10,12,15,16,18 is the same expression written in
the $z$–up convention $z\to h-z$; with the $z$ positive downwards
convention stated here the physically reported transfer function is the
$\sinh kh$ form above, $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi$ as
given, up to the usual $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ sign. ∎

$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
$\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$,

the material free surface $z=0$ in the steady state is
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}+kq_{0}=0$, and with
$z$ positive downwards

$\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$.

The free-surface normal stress is therefore
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ and with
$\Phi(z)=p_{1}z\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$,

$\Phi'''(0)= -2k^{3}q_{0}$,
so that on the hydrostatic balance $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}$.

The zero normal traction at the base is
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, which with the above $\Phi$ gives the
usual relation
$q_{1}=q_{0}\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$.

Evaluating the shear stress at the base,
$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2\big[p_{1}k\sinh kz+p_{1}zk^{2}\cosh kz
+q_{0}k^{2}\sinh kz+q_{1}k\cosh kz+q_{1}zk^{2}\sinh kz\big]$,
and with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ and the $q_{1}$ relation above,

$\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
  =-\,\frac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]
    \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}\;,$

i.e. up to the conventional $z\!\to\!h\!-\!z$ sign the shear
condition $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0},$

is

$q_{0}= -\frac{S_{0}h}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}
        \sinh kh$ ,

the $\sinh kh$ being the part of $\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi$ that survives after the
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ elimination.  Inserting this $q_{0}$ in
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}$ gives in magnitude

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
      \frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e. with $s=kh$

$e_{s}= \chi(s)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\displaystyle\chi(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}$,

written with a $\cosh$ after the $z\to h-z$ reflection, which is the
origin of the $\cosh$-numerator form quoted by Colleagues 1,10,12,16,18.

the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ under the stated free-surface,

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady Stokes stream-function problem for a harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ in an incompressible viscous layer $0\le z\le h$ with $z$ positive downwards gives with $\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.
The free surface $z=0$ is material in the steady state so $u_{z}(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ with $\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi'$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]$.
The base $z=h$ is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.
With $\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$ the top conditions give $p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$. Then $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $q_{1}=q_{0}[k\tanh kh-1/h]$ and the basal shear gives
$q_{0}=-S_{0}h\cosh kh/[2\mu k(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)]$.
The surface normal stress is $\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}q_{0}$, i.e.

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,k h\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$,

up to sign. In the isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi(kh)=k h\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]
=[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh]^{-1}$,
the sign being the $90^{\circ}$ phase between the $\sin kx$ basal traction and the $\cos kx$ topography. With $\cosh kh\simeq1$,
$\chi_{0}\simeq kh/(1+k^{2}h^{2})\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$, and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.

Majority of colleagues 1,10,12,16,18,7 obtain this $kh\cosh kh/(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)$ transfer function. Colleagues 2,8,9,14,15 quote the same function with $\sinh$ in the numerator, $\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$, which is the $z\to h-z$ interchange under the $z$ positive upwards geophysical convention. The $z$ sign is purely conventional; magnitude is identical.

Discrepant long-wave results $\chi\simeq3/2(kh)^{-1}$ or $\chi\simeq s/[\cosh s+s\sinh s]$ correspond to an impermeable base $w(h)=0$ or to a different normalisation of the basal shear, $f''(h)=S_{0}/\mu$ vs $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]$. The $3/2(kh)^{-1}$ lubrication limit is the impermeable-base/dynamic-topography limit, not the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ free-base limit stated.

Unresolved normalisation issues remain: factor 2 from $\eta$ vs $\mu$, and whether the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio is absorbed in $\chi$. The core $kh$-dependent transfer function is robustly $\chi(kh)\propto kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ tending to $kh$ for long waves, with the $\sinh$ form being the same expression under the opposite $z$ convention. With the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ the quoted stable amplitude is $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation is now stable around the Stokes stream-function solution for a 2-D incompressible viscous layer $0\le z\le h$ with a harmonic basal shear $\tau_b=S_0\sin kx$, $k=2\pi/\lambda$, free-surface kinematics $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$ in the steady state and normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$.

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, 
$\Phi=(p_0+p_1z)\cosh kz+(q_0+q_1z)\sinh kz$.

The material free surface in steady state gives $\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $p_0=0$, $p_1=-kq_0$, 
$\Phi(z)=q_0[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q_1z\sinh kz$.
The stresses in normal mode are
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,
$p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives
$q_1=q_0\big[k\tanh kh-1/h\big]$.
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ then gives

$q_0=-\frac{S_0 h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]}$,

up to the usual $S_0$ normalisation sign. The free-surface normal stress is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ with
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^3 q_0$, so that in magnitude

$\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^2 q_0
      =\frac{S_0\,k h\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}$.

Hence with the isostatic restoring stress written as $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_s =\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi(kh)=\frac{k h\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}
       =\Big[\frac{k h}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{k h}\Big]^{-1}$,
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$ being absorbed in sign, i.e. $e_s=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with the conventional sign.

Thin-sheet / long-wave limit $s=kh\ll1$, $\cosh s\simeq1$:
$\chi(s)=\frac{s}{1+s^2}+O(s^3)\approx s$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, often quoted as $e_s\simeq \frac{kh}{1+k^2h^2}\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}$.
For $s\gg1$, $\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$.

Disagreements in the round are essentially coordinate / normalisation variants.

* Colleagues 1,10,12,15,16,18 consistently give the cosh-numerator form above, i.e. $z$ positive downwards, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.
* Colleagues 2,8,9,13,14 note the $z\to h-z$ reflection which maps $\cosh\to\cosh$, $\sinh\to-\sinh$ in the basal shear coupling. With the physical geophysical convention $z$ positive upward the transfer function is written as
$\chi_{\rm up}(s)=s\sinh s/[s^2+\cosh^2 s]$,
$e_s=\chi_{\rm up}S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
which is the same function up to the even/odd interchange. In the $s\ll1$ limit this still gives $e_s\propto s\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ up to $O(1)$ normalisation.
* The impermeable-base $w(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$, variant gives the well known lubrication form
$\chi_i(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{\sinh s\cosh s-s}=s/[\cosh s-s\csch s]$,
with $\chi_i\simeq3/(2s)$ for $s\ll1$, i.e. $e_s\simeq 3S_0/(2kh\Delta\rho g)$. This is the Colleague 11,17 result and is obtained when no-penetration at the base is imposed in addition to $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.
* Several authors absorb a factor $1/2$ in the definition of $S_0$; the dimensionless functional form $s\cosh s/[s^2+\cosh^2 s]$ is robust, the numerical prefactor depends on whether $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]$ is normalised with $2\mu$ etc.

The sign / density identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ is a trivial rescaling. The essential stable steady response is the $kh$-dependent transfer function above, linear in $S_0$, decaying for short waves and $\chi\approx kh$ for long waves. That is the consensus magnitude; the remaining dispute is the $\cosh$ vs $\sinh$ numerator, which is purely the $z$ up/down convention, and the impermeable-base $3/(2kh)$ long-wave limit.

Unresolved: exact $1/2$ normalisation of $S_0$ in different papers; final sign convention for the $90^{\circ}$ phase. The magnitude quoted by the majority is $\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$, with the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor absorbed as per statement.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic stream function solution is the common core.
With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, 
$(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $D=d/dz$, $z$ positive downwards,

$\Phi(z)=(p_0+p_1z)\cosh kz+(q_0+q_1z)\sinh kz$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.

Material steady free surface $z=0$ : $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$ $\iff$ 
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ i.e. $p_0=0$, $p_1=-kq_0$.

Then in the $z$–down convention
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^3q_0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$,

so with the isostatic balance $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
$ \Delta\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^2q_0$.

Base $z=h$ : $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives
$(q_0+q_1h)\cosh kh+p_1h\sinh kh=0$, i.e.

$q_1=q_0\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$,

and the prescribed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$,

$\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$,

gives on the $p_1=-kq_0$ branch

$q_0=-\,\dfrac{S_0h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$.

Hence in magnitude

$\rho g e_s =\dfrac{S_0kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

and with the buoyancy density $\Delta\rho$

$e_s=\chi(kh)\dfrac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\displaystyle\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}$,
$s=kh$,

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$ being a sign,
conventionally $e_s=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$.  In particular

$\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}\to s$ for $s\ll1$,
$\chi(s)\sim s e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$,

so that $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh/(1+k^{2}h^{2})\approx kh$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$, the familiar thin–sheet
dynamic topography.  With $\cosh kh\simeq1$ this is often quoted as
$\chi_0=kh/(1+k^{2}h^{2})$.

Variants in the thread are conventional:
* $z$ up–down reflection changes $\cosh$ numerator to $\sinh$,
  $ \chi_{\rm up}=s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$, the $s\cosh s$ form being
  the same expression in the $z$ downwards convention used above.
* Imposing an extra impermeable base $u_z(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ gives the
  textbook lubrication transfer function
  $\chi_i(s)=s\sinh s/[\sinh s\cosh s-s]=s/[\cosh s-s\,{\rm csch}s]$,
  $ \chi_i\simeq3/2s$ for $s\ll1$, i.e. $e_s\simeq3S_0/(2kh\Delta\rho g)$.
  This is the form quoted by Colleagues 5,11,17, etc. It is not the
  problem as stated, which only imposes $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$
  and no normal velocity condition at the base.
* Sign/normalisation differences of $1/2$ and $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
  are conventional.

Current belief: for the stated free–base, material free surface problem
the stable steady amplitude in magnitude is $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$
with $\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^2+\cosh^2kh]$, $\chi\approx kh$ for
$kh\ll1$.  The sign is $e_s\propto-\,\mathrm{sgn}S_0$ expressing the
$90^{\circ}$ phase shift.  If the geophysical $z$ up convention is kept
the same function is written with $\sinh$ in the numerator.  The
impermeable–base $3/2s$ limit is a distinct physical assumption.

12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ is the
common framework. $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
$\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$,
with $z$ positive downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base.

Free material surface in the steady state: $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$,
i.e. $\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ $\Rightarrow p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$.
With the $2\mu$ Stokes convention

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ gives
$\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}$.

Base: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives $q_{1}=q_{0}[k\tanh kh-1/h]$.
With $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ the shear condition yields

$q_{0}= -\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,

and

$\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
 =\dfrac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

Hence in magnitude with the isostatic restoring $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
 =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,
$s=kh$, the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in sign.

Long wave: $\cosh kh\simeq1$,
$\chi\simeq kh/(1+k^{2}h^{2})\approx kh$, 
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi\to kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

This is the majority result of Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18.
The $\sinh$ numerator forms
$\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ reported by Colleagues
2,8,9,13,14 are the same expression under the $z\to h-z$ reflection,
i.e. $z$ positive upwards, and/or after imposing the extra no-penetration
$\Phi(h)=0$ condition. The impermeable-base $V(h)=0$ limit gives
$\chi_{i}=s\sinh s/[\sinh s\cosh s-s]\simeq 3/(2s)$ for $s\ll1$,
Colleague 5's $w(h)=0$ derivation. Those variants correspond to different
base kinematic assumptions, not the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$u_{z}(0)=0$ free-base problem.

The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density-ratio factor is inessential with the
convention $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ used in the statement. The stable
steady amplitude is the $kh$-dependent transfer function above, linear in
$kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponentially cut off for $kh\gg1$. ∎

16.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ with $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$ is the common starting point. Material steady free surface $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $p_0=0$, $p_1=-kq_0$ in $\Phi=(p_0+p_1z)\cosh kz+(q_0+q_1z)\sinh kz$ with $z$ positive down. 

With the $2\mu$ convention
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$, 
$p= -\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.

Free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives
$q_1=q_0[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}]$.
Basal shear $\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$ then yields
$q_0=-S_0 h\cosh kh/[2\mu k\,(k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh)]$
and $p_1=-kq_0$.

Surface normal stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ with
$\Phi'''(0)=3k^2p_1+k^3q_0=-2k^3q_0$.
Hence in steady state
$\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^2q_0
 =S_0 k h\cosh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]$.

In magnitude with the isostatic balance $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_s =\chi(s)S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with $s=kh$
$\chi(s)= s\cosh s/[s^2+\cosh^2 s]=[s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s]^{-1}$.
Long wave $s\ll1$: $\cosh s\simeq1$, $\chi\simeq s/(1+s^2)\approx s$,
so $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ and $\chi\to s e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$.
The $90^\circ$ phase is $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$, i.e. $e_s= -\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ in sign convention.

Disagreements noted in the round:
* Colleagues 2,8,9,13,14, and to some extent 5, obtain a $\sinh$ numerator $\chi(s)=s\sinh s/[s^2+\cosh^2 s]$, which is the same biharmonic solution expressed with the geophysical $z$ up convention $z\to h-z$ or under the extra condition $\Phi(h)=0$, $w(h)=0$. That is the impermeable/no-penetration base form.
* Colleague 5's no-penetration $w(h)=0$ gives the lubrication transfer $\chi(s)=s\sinh s/[\sinh s\cosh s-s]$ $\approx 3/2s^{-1}$ for $s\ll1$.
* Factors $1/2$, $ \rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$, and sign are consistently absorbed differently. The core $k h$-dependent viscous transfer is $s\cosh s/[s^2+\cosh^2 s]$, i.e. $\chi\sim s$ for thin plates and exponential decay for $s\gg1$. The $\sinh$ version is the $z$-reflection of the same function.

Remaining open: precise normalisation of $S_0$ as $\sigma_{xz}$ vs $2\mu\partial_z u_x$, and the exact sign convention in the statement $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$. Magnitude is as above; sign is opposite to $S_0$ due to the $90^\circ$ phase.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady Stokes normal mode is $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $\Phi(z)=(p0+p1z)\cosh kz+(q0+q1z)\sinh kz$. 
With a material free surface in the steady state $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$ i.e. $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ so $p0=0$, $p1=-kq0$. With the $2\mu$ Stokes stresses

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives $q1=q0\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$.
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S0$ then gives

$q0=-\dfrac{S0 h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]}$,

and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ with $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^3q0$,
so in magnitude

$\rho g e_s = -2\mu k^{2}q0 =\dfrac{S0 kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

Hence with the isostatic restoring $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_s=\chi(kh)\dfrac{S0}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
 =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$ being absorbed in sign. 
For $kh\ll1$, $\cosh kh\simeq1$, $\chi\simeq kh/(1+k^{2}h^{2})\approx kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S0/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\sim kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$. This is the cosh-numerator finite-thickness transfer function obtained by Colleagues 1,10,12,15,16,17,18,7.

Round-1 discussion shows the same expression reappears with the $\sinh$ numerator in Colleagues 2,8,9,14,13. That is the $z\to h-z$ / $z$ up vs $z$ down convention: with $z$ positive downwards the numerator is $\cosh kh$, with the geophysical $z$ up convention the equivalent physical transfer function is written as $kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$. The two are the same up to sign/orientation.

A distinct family, Colleagues 5,11,17 and the impermeable-base derivations, imposes $w(h)=0$ i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$ in addition to $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. That gives $q1=q0\big[k\coth kh-h^{-1}\big]$ and

$\chi_i(kh)=\dfrac{kh\sinh kh}{\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh}
 =\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh-kh\csch kh}$,
with the long-wave limit $\chi_i\simeq3/2kh^{-1}$, i.e. $e_s\simeq\frac32 S0/(kh\Delta\rho g)$. This is the lubrication / no-penetration limit, not the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ free-base problem.

The $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ factor is conventional: the surface balance is written as $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e$, sometimes quoted as $\rho g e$ with $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ absorbed in $\chi$. Sign is conventional $e_s=-\chi S0/\Delta\rho g$.

Unresolved normalisation details remain: factor $1/2$ from $2\mu$ vs $\mu$ stress definitions and the exact $\sinh$ vs $\cosh$ presentation, but the functional form $kh\,\text{hyperbolic}/[k^{2}h^{2}+\text{hyperbolic}^{2}]$ with linear $kh$ thin-plate limit is the stable steady amplitude under the stated $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S0\sin kx$ boundary-value problem.

15.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The 2-D Stokes layer $0\le z\le h$, $z$ positive downwards, is written with $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$.  Incompressibility gives $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$.

$\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0\iff p_{0}=0,\;p_{1}+kq_{0}=0$,

up to rigid body.  With the usual $2\mu$ stresses

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,

so that at the free surface $\Phi'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$.

With $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$,
$\Phi(z)=q_{0}[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q_{1}z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx$.

Base: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives

$q_{1}=q_{0}\big[\,k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$,
and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ gives

$q_{0}= -\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$.

Hence in the steady $de/dt\to0$ limit

$\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
          =\dfrac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e. in magnitude

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,\chi_{\rho}(s)$,
$\chi_{\rho}(s)=\dfrac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Big[\,s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s\Big]^{-1}$,
$s=kh$.

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_{s}= \chi(s)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(s)=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$,
up to the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$,
conventionally $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

Thin–long wave $s\ll1$, $\cosh s\simeq1$:

$\chi(s)=\dfrac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3})\approx s$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
often quoted as $e_{s}\simeq S_{0}kh/[\Delta\rho g(1+k^{2}h^{2})]$.
$\chi\to s e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$.

Disagreement noted in the deliberation:

* Colleagues 2,8,9,14 obtain a $\sinh s$ numerator,
$\chi_{s}=s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$, which is the same biharmonic
solution written with the geophysical $z$ positive upwards, i.e. the
$z\to h-z$ reflection $\cosh\leftrightarrow\sinh$ in the surface
coupling.  The physics is the same up to sign/convention.

* Colleagues 11,14,17 impose an impermeable/no net flux base
$w(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$, giving the sealed-channel transfer function
$\chi_{i}(s)=s\sinh s/[\sinh s\cosh s-s]=s/[\cosh s-s\,{\rm csch}s]$,
with the long wave lubrication limit $\chi_{i}\simeq3/(2s)$.
That is a different physical base condition and is not the
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ free-base problem stated.

The majority 1,10,12,16,18 agree on the finite-thickness transfer
function above.  The factor $1/2$ differences are a $\mu$ vs $\eta=2\mu$
normalisation of $S_{0}$ and do not change the dimensionless $s$
dependence.  The sign is a $90^{\circ}$ phase convention; the magnitude
is the $\chi(s)$ quoted.  The density contrast $\Delta\rho$ is the
relevant restoring density for the free-surface balance.

reflection_text.3:
The steady Stokes stream-function problem for a harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ in an incompressible viscous layer $0\le z\le h$ with $z$ positive downwards gives with $\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.
The free surface $z=0$ is material in the steady state so $u_{z}(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ with $\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi'$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]$.
The base $z=h$ is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.
With $\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$ the top conditions give $p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$. Then $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $q_{1}=q_{0}[k\tanh kh-1/h]$ and the basal shear gives
$q_{0}=-S_{0}h\cosh kh/[2\mu k(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)]$.
The surface normal stress is $\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}q_{0}$, i.e.

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,k h\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$,

up to sign. In the isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi(kh)=k h\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]
=[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh]^{-1}$,
the sign being the $90^{\circ}$ phase between the $\sin kx$ basal traction and the $\cos kx$ topography. With $\cosh kh\simeq1$,
$\chi_{0}\simeq kh/(1+k^{2}h^{2})\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$, and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.

Majority of colleagues 1,10,12,16,18,7 obtain this $kh\cosh kh/(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)$ transfer function. Colleagues 2,8,9,14,15 quote the same function with $\sinh$ in the numerator, $\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$, which is the $z\to h-z$ interchange under the $z$ positive upwards geophysical convention. The $z$ sign is purely conventional; magnitude is identical.

Discrepant long-wave results $\chi\simeq3/2(kh)^{-1}$ or $\chi\simeq s/[\cosh s+s\sinh s]$ correspond to an impermeable base $w(h)=0$ or to a different normalisation of the basal shear, $f''(h)=S_{0}/\mu$ vs $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]$. The $3/2(kh)^{-1}$ lubrication limit is the impermeable-base/dynamic-topography limit, not the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ free-base limit stated.

Unresolved normalisation issues remain: factor 2 from $\eta$ vs $\mu$, and whether the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio is absorbed in $\chi$. The core $kh$-dependent transfer function is robustly $\chi(kh)\propto kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ tending to $kh$ for long waves, with the $\sinh$ form being the same expression under the opposite $z$ convention. With the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ the quoted stable amplitude is $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.
reflection_text.1:
The deliberation is now stable around the Stokes stream-function solution for a 2-D incompressible viscous layer $0\le z\le h$ with a harmonic basal shear $\tau_b=S_0\sin kx$, $k=2\pi/\lambda$, free-surface kinematics $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$ in the steady state and normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$.

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, 
$\Phi=(p_0+p_1z)\cosh kz+(q_0+q_1z)\sinh kz$.

The material free surface in steady state gives $\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $p_0=0$, $p_1=-kq_0$, 
$\Phi(z)=q_0[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q_1z\sinh kz$.
The stresses in normal mode are
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,
$p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives
$q_1=q_0\big[k\tanh kh-1/h\big]$.
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ then gives

$q_0=-\frac{S_0 h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]}$,

up to the usual $S_0$ normalisation sign. The free-surface normal stress is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ with
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^3 q_0$, so that in magnitude

$\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^2 q_0
      =\frac{S_0\,k h\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}$.

Hence with the isostatic restoring stress written as $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_s =\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi(kh)=\frac{k h\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}
       =\Big[\frac{k h}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{k h}\Big]^{-1}$,
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$ being absorbed in sign, i.e. $e_s=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with the conventional sign.

Thin-sheet / long-wave limit $s=kh\ll1$, $\cosh s\simeq1$:
$\chi(s)=\frac{s}{1+s^2}+O(s^3)\approx s$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, often quoted as $e_s\simeq \frac{kh}{1+k^2h^2}\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}$.
For $s\gg1$, $\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$.

Disagreements in the round are essentially coordinate / normalisation variants.

* Colleagues 1,10,12,15,16,18 consistently give the cosh-numerator form above, i.e. $z$ positive downwards, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.
* Colleagues 2,8,9,13,14 note the $z\to h-z$ reflection which maps $\cosh\to\cosh$, $\sinh\to-\sinh$ in the basal shear coupling. With the physical geophysical convention $z$ positive upward the transfer function is written as
$\chi_{\rm up}(s)=s\sinh s/[s^2+\cosh^2 s]$,
$e_s=\chi_{\rm up}S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
which is the same function up to the even/odd interchange. In the $s\ll1$ limit this still gives $e_s\propto s\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ up to $O(1)$ normalisation.
* The impermeable-base $w(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$, variant gives the well known lubrication form
$\chi_i(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{\sinh s\cosh s-s}=s/[\cosh s-s\csch s]$,
with $\chi_i\simeq3/(2s)$ for $s\ll1$, i.e. $e_s\simeq 3S_0/(2kh\Delta\rho g)$. This is the Colleague 11,17 result and is obtained when no-penetration at the base is imposed in addition to $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.
* Several authors absorb a factor $1/2$ in the definition of $S_0$; the dimensionless functional form $s\cosh s/[s^2+\cosh^2 s]$ is robust, the numerical prefactor depends on whether $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]$ is normalised with $2\mu$ etc.

The sign / density identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ is a trivial rescaling. The essential stable steady response is the $kh$-dependent transfer function above, linear in $S_0$, decaying for short waves and $\chi\approx kh$ for long waves. That is the consensus magnitude; the remaining dispute is the $\cosh$ vs $\sinh$ numerator, which is purely the $z$ up/down convention, and the impermeable-base $3/(2kh)$ long-wave limit.

Unresolved: exact $1/2$ normalisation of $S_0$ in different papers; final sign convention for the $90^{\circ}$ phase. The magnitude quoted by the majority is $\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$, with the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor absorbed as per statement.
reflection_text.6:
The biharmonic stream function solution is the common core.
With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, 
$(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $D=d/dz$, $z$ positive downwards,

$\Phi(z)=(p_0+p_1z)\cosh kz+(q_0+q_1z)\sinh kz$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.

Material steady free surface $z=0$ : $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$ $\iff$ 
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ i.e. $p_0=0$, $p_1=-kq_0$.

Then in the $z$–down convention
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^3q_0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$,

so with the isostatic balance $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
$ \Delta\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^2q_0$.

Base $z=h$ : $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives
$(q_0+q_1h)\cosh kh+p_1h\sinh kh=0$, i.e.

$q_1=q_0\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$,

and the prescribed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$,

$\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$,

gives on the $p_1=-kq_0$ branch

$q_0=-\,\dfrac{S_0h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$.

Hence in magnitude

$\rho g e_s =\dfrac{S_0kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

and with the buoyancy density $\Delta\rho$

$e_s=\chi(kh)\dfrac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\displaystyle\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}$,
$s=kh$,

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$ being a sign,
conventionally $e_s=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$.  In particular

$\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}\to s$ for $s\ll1$,
$\chi(s)\sim s e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$,

so that $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh/(1+k^{2}h^{2})\approx kh$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$, the familiar thin–sheet
dynamic topography.  With $\cosh kh\simeq1$ this is often quoted as
$\chi_0=kh/(1+k^{2}h^{2})$.

Variants in the thread are conventional:
* $z$ up–down reflection changes $\cosh$ numerator to $\sinh$,
  $ \chi_{\rm up}=s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$, the $s\cosh s$ form being
  the same expression in the $z$ downwards convention used above.
* Imposing an extra impermeable base $u_z(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ gives the
  textbook lubrication transfer function
  $\chi_i(s)=s\sinh s/[\sinh s\cosh s-s]=s/[\cosh s-s\,{\rm csch}s]$,
  $ \chi_i\simeq3/2s$ for $s\ll1$, i.e. $e_s\simeq3S_0/(2kh\Delta\rho g)$.
  This is the form quoted by Colleagues 5,11,17, etc. It is not the
  problem as stated, which only imposes $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$
  and no normal velocity condition at the base.
* Sign/normalisation differences of $1/2$ and $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
  are conventional.

Current belief: for the stated free–base, material free surface problem
the stable steady amplitude in magnitude is $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$
with $\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^2+\cosh^2kh]$, $\chi\approx kh$ for
$kh\ll1$.  The sign is $e_s\propto-\,\mathrm{sgn}S_0$ expressing the
$90^{\circ}$ phase shift.  If the geophysical $z$ up convention is kept
the same function is written with $\sinh$ in the numerator.  The
impermeable–base $3/2s$ limit is a distinct physical assumption.
reflection_text.12:
The biharmonic stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ is the
common framework. $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
$\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$,
with $z$ positive downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base.

Free material surface in the steady state: $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$,
i.e. $\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ $\Rightarrow p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$.
With the $2\mu$ Stokes convention

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ gives
$\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}$.

Base: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives $q_{1}=q_{0}[k\tanh kh-1/h]$.
With $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ the shear condition yields

$q_{0}= -\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,

and

$\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
 =\dfrac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

Hence in magnitude with the isostatic restoring $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
 =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,
$s=kh$, the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in sign.

Long wave: $\cosh kh\simeq1$,
$\chi\simeq kh/(1+k^{2}h^{2})\approx kh$, 
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi\to kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

This is the majority result of Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18.
The $\sinh$ numerator forms
$\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ reported by Colleagues
2,8,9,13,14 are the same expression under the $z\to h-z$ reflection,
i.e. $z$ positive upwards, and/or after imposing the extra no-penetration
$\Phi(h)=0$ condition. The impermeable-base $V(h)=0$ limit gives
$\chi_{i}=s\sinh s/[\sinh s\cosh s-s]\simeq 3/(2s)$ for $s\ll1$,
Colleague 5's $w(h)=0$ derivation. Those variants correspond to different
base kinematic assumptions, not the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$u_{z}(0)=0$ free-base problem.

The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density-ratio factor is inessential with the
convention $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ used in the statement. The stable
steady amplitude is the $kh$-dependent transfer function above, linear in
$kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponentially cut off for $kh\gg1$. ∎
reflection_text.16:
The biharmonic stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ with $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$ is the common starting point. Material steady free surface $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $p_0=0$, $p_1=-kq_0$ in $\Phi=(p_0+p_1z)\cosh kz+(q_0+q_1z)\sinh kz$ with $z$ positive down. 

With the $2\mu$ convention
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$, 
$p= -\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.

Free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives
$q_1=q_0[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}]$.
Basal shear $\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$ then yields
$q_0=-S_0 h\cosh kh/[2\mu k\,(k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh)]$
and $p_1=-kq_0$.

Surface normal stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ with
$\Phi'''(0)=3k^2p_1+k^3q_0=-2k^3q_0$.
Hence in steady state
$\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^2q_0
 =S_0 k h\cosh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]$.

In magnitude with the isostatic balance $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_s =\chi(s)S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with $s=kh$
$\chi(s)= s\cosh s/[s^2+\cosh^2 s]=[s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s]^{-1}$.
Long wave $s\ll1$: $\cosh s\simeq1$, $\chi\simeq s/(1+s^2)\approx s$,
so $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ and $\chi\to s e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$.
The $90^\circ$ phase is $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$, i.e. $e_s= -\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ in sign convention.

Disagreements noted in the round:
* Colleagues 2,8,9,13,14, and to some extent 5, obtain a $\sinh$ numerator $\chi(s)=s\sinh s/[s^2+\cosh^2 s]$, which is the same biharmonic solution expressed with the geophysical $z$ up convention $z\to h-z$ or under the extra condition $\Phi(h)=0$, $w(h)=0$. That is the impermeable/no-penetration base form.
* Colleague 5's no-penetration $w(h)=0$ gives the lubrication transfer $\chi(s)=s\sinh s/[\sinh s\cosh s-s]$ $\approx 3/2s^{-1}$ for $s\ll1$.
* Factors $1/2$, $ \rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$, and sign are consistently absorbed differently. The core $k h$-dependent viscous transfer is $s\cosh s/[s^2+\cosh^2 s]$, i.e. $\chi\sim s$ for thin plates and exponential decay for $s\gg1$. The $\sinh$ version is the $z$-reflection of the same function.

Remaining open: precise normalisation of $S_0$ as $\sigma_{xz}$ vs $2\mu\partial_z u_x$, and the exact sign convention in the statement $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$. Magnitude is as above; sign is opposite to $S_0$ due to the $90^\circ$ phase.
reflection_text.4:

 =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

reflection_text.15:
The 2-D Stokes layer $0\le z\le h$, $z$ positive downwards, is written with $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$.  Incompressibility gives $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$.

A material steady free surface at $z=0$ is $u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e.

$\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0\iff p_{0}=0,\;p_{1}+kq_{0}=0$,

up to rigid body.  With the usual $2\mu$ stresses

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,

so that at the free surface $\Phi'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$.

With $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$,
$\Phi(z)=q_{0}[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q_{1}z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx$.

Base: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives

$q_{1}=q_{0}\big[\,k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$,
and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ gives

$q_{0}= -\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$.

Hence in the steady $de/dt\to0$ limit

$\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
          =\dfrac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e. in magnitude

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,\chi_{\rho}(s)$,
$\chi_{\rho}(s)=\dfrac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Big[\,s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s\Big]^{-1}$,
$s=kh$.

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_{s}= \chi(s)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(s)=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$,
up to the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$,
conventionally $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

Thin–long wave $s\ll1$, $\cosh s\simeq1$:

$\chi(s)=\dfrac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3})\approx s$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
often quoted as $e_{s}\simeq S_{0}kh/[\Delta\rho g(1+k^{2}h^{2})]$.
$\chi\to s e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$.

Disagreement noted in the deliberation:

* Colleagues 2,8,9,14 obtain a $\sinh s$ numerator,
$\chi_{s}=s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$, which is the same biharmonic
solution written with the geophysical $z$ positive upwards, i.e. the
$z\to h-z$ reflection $\cosh\leftrightarrow\sinh$ in the surface
coupling.  The physics is the same up to sign/convention.

* Colleagues 11,14,17 impose an impermeable/no net flux base
$w(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$, giving the sealed-channel transfer function
$\chi_{i}(s)=s\sinh s/[\sinh s\cosh s-s]=s/[\cosh s-s\,{\rm csch}s]$,
with the long wave lubrication limit $\chi_{i}\simeq3/(2s)$.
That is a different physical base condition and is not the
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ free-base problem stated.

The majority 1,10,12,16,18 agree on the finite-thickness transfer
function above.  The factor $1/2$ differences are a $\mu$ vs $\eta=2\mu$
normalisation of $S_{0}$ and do not change the dimensionless $s$
dependence.  The sign is a $90^{\circ}$ phase convention; the magnitude
is the $\chi(s)$ quoted.  The density contrast $\Delta\rho$ is the
relevant restoring density for the free-surface balance.

The normal-mode Stokes problem is $ \psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ with $z\ge0$ downwards, top $z=0$, base $z=h$.
Steady material free surface $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. up to rigid mode
$\Phi =p_{1}z\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$.
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.
Base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ $\iff$ $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives
$q_{1}=q_{0}\big[k\tanh kh-1/h\big]$.
Basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ gives
$q_{0}= -S_{0}h\cosh kh/[2\mu k\big(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big)]$.
Surface normal stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ with $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}$,
so $\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}=S_{0}kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.
With the isostatic balance $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the $\rho$ is replaced by $\Delta\rho$ and in magnitude

$e_{s}= \chi(kh) S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
        =\Big[\,kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\,\Big]^{-1}$,

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$, i.e. $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ with the sign convention used. In the thin-sheet/long-wave limit $\cosh kh\simeq1$,
$\chi\simeq kh/(1+k^{2}h^{2})\approx kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.

The $\sinh$-numerator forms $\chi_{i}=kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ or $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ obtained by Colleagues 2,8,9,14,17 are the same expression written with the geophysical $z$ positive upwards, $z\to h-z$, i.e. $\cosh\leftrightarrow\sinh$ in the presentation, or with the extra impermeable/no-penetration condition $\Phi(h)=0$, $w(h)=0$. The $3/2kh^{-1}$ lubrication limit $e_{s}\simeq 3/(2kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is the $V(h)=0$/zero-mean-flux/no-penetration base normalisation and is not the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, free-penetration base. The $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ identification is a trivial density-ratio factor; with the usual notation $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ the dimensionless transfer function is the one above, up to sign. This is the stable $de/dt\to0$ steady response.

With a material free surface in steady state $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=0,\Phi'(0)=0$ and up to rigid body $\Phi(z)=p_1z\cosh kz+(q_0+q_1z)\sinh kz$ with $p_1=-kq_0$.  Stresses

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, $\quad\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,

the base conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ give $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ and

$q_1=q_0\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$.

The imposed shear then yields

$q_0=-\dfrac{S_0h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$.

With $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ and $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_0$,

$\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^{2}q_0=\dfrac{S_0kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

In magnitude, with the isostatic restoring $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_s=\chi(kh)\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_\rho(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
           =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

and with the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$, $\chi(kh)$ is the quoted transfer function.  Thin-plate: $\cosh kh\approx1$ gives

$\chi(kh)\simeq\dfrac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\approx kh$,

$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, decaying as $kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  The sign is the $90^\circ$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$, conventionally written $e_s=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

That gives $\chi_i=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$ and the long-wave lubrication limit $\chi\sim\frac32/(kh)$, i.e. $e_s\approx\frac32 S_0/(kh\Delta\rho g)$, quoted by Colleagues 5,11,17.  That form corresponds to no normal flow at the base, not the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ free base stated in the problem.

Unresolved normalisation issues persist: factor $2\mu$ vs $\mu$ in the stress definition, sign convention for the $90^\circ$ phase, and the $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ replacement in the free-surface balance.  The majority consensus for the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$, $u_x(0)=0$, steady $u_z(0)=0$ set-up with $z$ positive downwards is the $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ transfer function and thin-plate limit $\chi\approx kh$.

$\big(D^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0$,
$\Phi=(p_0+p_1z)\cosh kz+(q_0+q_1z)\sinh kz$.
For a steady material free surface $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$,
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ gives $p_0=0$, $p_1=-kq_0$ and

$\Phi(z)=-kq_0z\cosh kz+[q_0+q_1z]\sinh kz$.

With the $2\mu$ convention
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$, $\Phi'(0)=0$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_0$, so
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}q_0\cos kx$.
The stated free-surface balance is $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
hence on the quasi-static branch $\rho g e=-2\mu k^{2}q_0$.
In the isostatic form normally used the density is the contrast
$\Delta\rho$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ in $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

Stress-free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
i.e.
$(q_0+q_1h)\cosh kh+p_1h\sinh kh=0$,
with $p_1=-kq_0$
$q_1=q_0\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$.
The imposed basal shear
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$, $\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_h=S_0$, gives

$q_0=-\dfrac{S_0h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,
$p_1=-kq_0$.
Eliminating $q_0$,

$\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^{2}q_0
   =S_0\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e. in magnitude

$e_s=\chi_{\rho}(kh)\dfrac{S_0}{\rho g}$,
$\chi_{\rho}(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
 =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

and $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.
The sign is $e_s\propto -S_0$ according to the $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
