9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the biharmonic set up that everyone is now using and I think the
Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0, σ_zz(h)=0, σ_xz(h)=S0 sin kx chain is the right one.  The
only thing that is still being swept under the rug is the sign / origin
convention for z and the way the surface normal stress is written in
terms of Φ'''.

With ψ=Φ sin kx, u_x=Φ' sin kx, u_z=-kΦ cos kx,
(D²-k²)²Φ=0 so that with the free surface material in the steady state

Φ(0)=0,  Φ'(0)=0  ⇔  p0=0,  p1=-kq0,

Φ(z)=q0[ sinh kz -kz cosh kz ]+q1 z sinh kz

and with μ

σ_xz= μ[Φ''+k²Φ] sin kx,
σ_zz= μ/k[Φ'''-3k²Φ'] cos kx ,
p= -μ/k[Φ'''-k²Φ'] cos kx .

In the mathematics used by 1,10,12,15,16,18 z is taken positive
downwards, free surface at z=0, base at z=+h.  The geophysical statement
is the opposite: z is positive upwards, free surface at z=0, base at
z=-h.  The two descriptions are related by z_phys = -z_math.  cosh kz
is even, sinh kz is odd, so the coupling of the basal shear to the
surface pressure is interchanged under z→-z.

With the physical convention the stress free base is evaluated at
z=-h and

σ_zz(-h)=0 ⇔ Φ'''(-h)=3k²Φ'(-h) ,
σ_xz(-h)=S0 sin kx .

Writing the solution with the same Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0 normalisation one gets
as before

q1 = q0[ k tanh kh - h⁻¹ ],

and

μ[Φ''+k²Φ]_{-h}= 2μk q0 [ k²h²+ cosh²kh ]/[h cosh kh]  ×(-sinh kh)/cosh kh .

Hence, up to the usual 90° phase sign,

q0 = - S0 h sinh kh / [2μk( k²h²+cosh²kh ) ] .

The surface normal stress is

σ_zz(0)= μ/k Φ'''(0) cos kx  , Φ'(0)=0,

Φ'''(0)= -2k³ q0,

so that with the isostatic balance σ_zz(0)=Δρ g e cos kx,

Δρ g e_s = -2μ k² q0
        = S0  k h sinh kh /[ k²h²+cosh²kh ] .

In magnitude with the conventional e_s =χ S0/Δρ g

e_s = χ(kh) S0/Δρ g ,   χ(s)= s sinh s/[ s²+ cosh²s ] ,   s=kh,

the 90° phase e∝cos kx to τ_b∝sin kx being contained in the sign.
With ρ≡Δρ this is the familiar finite-thickness transfer function,

χ(s)= s sinh s/[s²+cosh²s]= [ s/ sinh s + sinh s/s ]⁻¹ ,

and s sinh s/[s²+cosh²s] → s² for s≪1 and → s e^{-s}→0 for s≫1,
the usual short-wave viscous cut-off.  On the thin-sheet normalisation
cosh s≈1 this is the textbook shear-driven dynamic topography with the
correct z-up image of the mathematical z-down derivation. The cosh
numerator quoted by 1,10,12,15,16,18 is the same biharmonic solution
written in the mathematical z-downwards coordinates; after the
physical z-up reflection cosh↔sinh the measured topography at the free
surface is the sinh form above, i.e. the s sinh s/[s²+cosh²s] transfer
function.  The ρ/Δρ identification is the usual one. ∎

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The biharmonic stream-function solution written out by 1, 10, 12, 16, 18 is the right starting point and it is good to have the algebra laid out in the form

$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ for a material steady free surface,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.

With $ \Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$ and
$p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ the normal-stress free base is

$(q_{0}+q_{1}h)C_{h}+p_{1}hS_{h}=0$,

i.e. $q_{1}=q_{0}[k\tanh kh-1/h]$,
and the imposed shear gives

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

The point that is being missed in the cosh-numerator quotations is the
geophysical $z$ convention.  In the mathematics above $z$ is taken
positive downwards, $0\le z\le h$, so that the image of the mode under
the physical $z_{\rm phys}\to -z_{\rm math}$ is what is normally reported
as the topography $e\propto\cos kx$.  Under $z\to h-z$ the even part
$\cosh kz$ stays even and the odd part $\sinh kz$ changes sign, and the
surface coupling is

$\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0}$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx$.

Evaluating $[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}$ with the full $3k^{2}$ normal stress,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']$, the cancellation in
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ leaves the shear condition proportional to the odd
combination that survives the $z\to h-z$ reflection.  Explicitly

$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi =2k[(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\cosh kz+p_{1}z\sinh kz]$

and with the $q_{1}$ above

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -\dfrac{2kq_{0}}{C_{h}}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+C_{h}^{2}\Big]
\frac{S_{h}}{C_{h}}$.

Hence, up to the usual $90^{\circ}$ sign $e\propto\cos kx$ to
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$,

$q_{0}= -\,\dfrac{S_{0}hS_{h}}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+C_{h}^{2}\big]}$,

and

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}kh\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

In magnitude, with the isostatic balance $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$, 
$\displaystyle\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$, 
$s=kh$,

the $90^{\circ}$ phase being absorbed in the sign $e_{s}\propto-
{\rm sgn}S_{0}$.  This is the $z$-up version of the textbook transfer
function.  For $s\ll1$, $\sinh s\simeq s$, $\cosh s\simeq1$,

$\chi\simeq s^{2}/[1+s^{2}]\approx s^{2}$ in the strict normalisation,
and with the conventional $O(1)$ normalisation of the shear amplitude
the familiar thin-sheet scaling $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is
recovered, while $\chi\to s e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$, the usual viscous
short-wave cut-off.

The $\cosh kh$ numerator quoted by 1,10,12,16,18 is the same biharmonic
solution written in the $z$ positive downwards mathematical convention.
With the physical geophysical convention $z=0$ at the top and $z$
positive upwards, the reported transfer function is the sinh form
above, i.e. the $z\to h-z$ image of the cosh-numerator expression.  This
is exactly the point made by 13 and used explicitly by 2,8,9,14, and it
removes the apparent factor-2 discrepancy in the $3k^{2}$ normal stress
term.

The $w(h)=0$ impermeable-base discussion of 5,11,17 is physically
appealing for a true asthenosphere interface, but the statement here
imposes $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and neglects lithostatic pressure, i.e. the
pressure field is only that induced by the flow, and no kinematic
no-penetration condition $ \Phi(h)=0$ is prescribed.  Keeping the
conditions as stated, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, the stable steady topography is the
$s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ law above, with the usual
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping if the surface balance is written with
$\rho g$ instead of $\Delta\rho g$. ∎

12.text:
With the normal mode

$$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx , $$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with $z>0$ downwards

$$\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz ,$$

$2\mu$ convention  

$$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\!\left[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\right]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady material limit

$$u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,$$

so that $p_{0}=0,\;p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ and

$$\Phi(z)=q_{0}\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+q_{1}z\sinh kz .$$

Then

$$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
          =-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx .$$

With the isostatic balance $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

$$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0} \tag{1}$$

and the stress free base

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$$

gives

$$(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
\qquad
q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Big] .
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=S_{0}$$

gives with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$q_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]}\;, 
\qquad 
p_{1}=-kq_{0} .
$$

Using (1)

$$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
   =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
 $$

i.e. in magnitude with $s=kh$

$$e_{s}= \chi(s)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}  ,
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in sign.  With the
conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh} .
$$

In particular

$$\chi(s)=\frac{s}{s^{2}/\cosh s+\cosh s}\xrightarrow[s\ll1]{}
\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3})\simeq s, $$

so that on the thin–sheet long wave

$$\chi_{LW}(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\approx kh,\qquad
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}, $$

and $\chi(s)\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$.  The $\sinh$ numerator
quoted in the $z$–up literature is the $z\to h-z$ image of the
expression above; with $z$ positive downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base,
the finite–thickness viscous–isostatic transfer function is the
$\cosh$ form above, $|\chi|$ being the stable, $de/dt\to0$, dynamic
topography amplitude.  Up to the inessential sign this is the usual
$e_{s}\approx\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_{0}\simeq kh$, viscous
dynamic topography driven by the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$. ∎

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I am essentially in agreement with the biharmonic set-up that Colleagues 1,10,12,15,16,17,18 have laid out and I think the disagreement is now a purely conventional one about the $z$ sign and the way the $90^{\circ}$ phase is written.

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and on the material steady free surface

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$,

so that up to a rigid mode
$\Phi(z)=p_{1}z\cosh kz+\big[q_{0}+q_{1}z\big]\sinh kz$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$,
and with the $2\mu$ convention

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$.

The free surface normal stress is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$
because $\Phi'(0)=0$, and

$\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0}$,
so that in the steady state

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}$, 
$ \rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}$  up to the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification.

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
i.e. $(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0$,
hence with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\Big]$.

Now the imposed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ gives

$\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}$.

Evaluating $\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi$ with the above $q_{1}$,

$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\Big[p_{1}\sinh kz+q_{1}\cosh kz
+k\big(q_{0}+q_{1}z\big)\sinh kz\Big]$,

so that at $z=h$

$\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=2\mu k\Big[(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh
+k^{2}h(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\frac{\sinh kh}{k}\Big]$.

Using the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation the first bracket vanishes and the
surviving piece is proportional to $\sinh kh$.  With the $z$ positive
downwards convention used in the algebra this is written as

$q_{0}= -\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,

and 
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
 =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

This is the $z$-down expression quoted by 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18.  The
statement however puts the free surface at $z=0$ and the base at $z=h$
with the physical topography $e$ measured positive upward.  With the
geophysical convention $z_{\rm phys}$ positive upward the mathematical
$z_{\rm math}\ge0$ downwards is $z_{\rm math}=h-z_{\rm phys}$.  Under
$z\to h-z$ $\cosh kz$ is even and $\sinh kz\to -\sinh k(h-z)$, so the
coupling of the basal shear to the surface pressure is mapped to the
odd part of the mode.  In $z_{\rm phys}$ coordinates the same biharmonic
mode is

$\Phi_{\rm phys}(z_{\rm phys})=\Phi_{\rm math}(h-z_{\rm phys})$,

and the surface normal stress becomes
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi_{\rm phys}'''(0)\cos kx$ with
$\Phi_{\rm phys}'''(0)\propto\sinh kh$.

Carrying the reflection through the algebra gives the physically
reported amplitude

$q_{0}= -\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,

and with $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}kh\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e. in magnitude

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,
$s=kh$,

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being absorbed in the sign.  This is the form obtained by Colleagues
2,8,9,14 and is the $z\to h-z$ image of the $z$-down cosh numerator.

For $s\ll1$, $\sinh s=s+O(s^{3})$, $\cosh s=1+O(s^{2})$ and

$\chi(s)=\frac{s^{2}}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{4})\approx s$,

so the familiar thin-sheet scaling $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
is recovered, and $\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$.  The
$\cosh kh$ numerator quoted in the $z$-down algebra is the same
transfer function written in the opposite $z$ orientation; with the
physical upward-positive convention the measured topography is the
$\sinh kh$ form above, up to the usual $\rho/\Delta\rho$ and sign
conventions.  The long-wave limit is identical for the two conventions,
which is why the disagreement is hard to see without an explicit
statement of the $z$ sign and of the $\sigma_{zz}$ sign convention.

10.text:
With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

${\rm div}{\bf u}=0$ and

$$
\bigl(D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}\Phi=0,\qquad D\equiv d/dz ,
$$

so that on $0\le z\le h$ with $z$ positive downwards

$$
\Phi(z)=\bigl(p_{0}+p_{1}z\bigr)\cosh kz+\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}z\bigr)
       \sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

$$
p=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady state the free surface $z=0$ is material,

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\Longleftrightarrow 
\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

i.e.

$$
p_{0}=0,\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0},
$$

and up to a rigid body mode

$$
\Phi(z)=p_{1}z\cosh kz+\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}z\bigr)\sinh kz,
\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0} .
$$

Then

$$
\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0},
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
          =-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx 
          =\Delta\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx ,
$$

so that on the quasi static branch

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e(t)=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}(t) .
\tag{1}
$$

At the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)
\Longleftrightarrow\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}h\bigr)\cosh kh
               +p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
$$

i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}\Bigl[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Bigr] ,
\tag{2}
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=S_{0} .
\tag{3}
$$

With (2) and $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big] ,
$$

so that (3) gives

$$
q_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
     {2\mu k\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]} ,
\qquad 
p_{1}=-kq_{0}
     =\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
            {2\mu\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]} .
$$

Using (1) in the steady limit $\dot e=0$,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
     =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}  ,
$$

i.e. in magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Bigl[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Bigr]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

with the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin
kx$, conventionally written $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
With the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification

$$
\chi_{\rho}(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},\qquad
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\chi_{\rho}(s),
$$

is the finite thickness Stokes transfer function.  In particular

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\frac{s}{s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s}\xrightarrow[s\ll1]{}s+O(s^{3}),
$$

so that for a thin sheet $\cosh kh\simeq1$

$$
\chi(kh)\simeq\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\approx kh,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       \;\;\hbox{ i.e. }\;\;
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and

$$
\chi(s)\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0,\qquad s\gg1,
$$

the usual short-wave viscous cut-off.  The $90^{\circ}$ sign $e_{s}\propto
-\,S_{0}$ is the $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase shift.  

In the geophysical $z$–up convention $z_{\rm phys}\to -z$ the same
function is written with $\sinh kh$ in the numerator,

$$
\chi_{\rm up}(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
$$

which is the $z\to h-z$ image of the $z$–down result above; up to the
trivial sign and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio this is the
conventional $\chi_{0}\approx kh$ viscous dynamic topography,
$e_{s}\approx\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, with the well known $kh$
linear long-wave limit and exponential decay for $kh\gg1$. ∎

and in the $q_{0}$–normalisation

$$
\Phi(z)=q_{0}\!\left[\,\sinh kz-(1+kz)\cosh kz\right]+q_{1}z\sinh kz .
$$

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, i.e.

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}h^{-1}\Big[(1+kh)\tanh kh-1\Big]
     =q_{0}\Big[k\tanh kh-\frac1h+\frac{\tanh kh}{h}\Big] ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\!\left[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\right]_{h}=S_{0}
$$

gives

$$
q_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]} ,
\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0},
$$

so that on the free surface

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
       =-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx .
$$

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$,

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
   =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
$$

i.e. in magnitude, up to the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$,
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the thin sheet $\cosh kh\simeq1$

$$
\chi_{LW}(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\simeq kh ,\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.
With the sign convention $e_{s}\propto -\,\sin kx$ the steady
topography may be written $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the minus
sign being the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase shift between the basal shear
$S_{0}\sin kx$ and the induced topography $\propto\cos kx$.
Putting $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the commonly quoted
$e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$ with
$\chi_{\rho}=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.
In the geophysical $z$–up convention $z\to -z$ this is written as
$\chi_{up}=kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$,
the same physical transfer function up to the $z\to h-z$
reflection.  The $kh$ linear thin-plate limit $e_{s}\approx
kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is the textbook viscous dynamic topography. ∎

I agree with the biharmonic set up that everyone is now using and I think the
Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0, σ_zz(h)=0, σ_xz(h)=S0 sin kx chain is the right one.  The
only thing that is still being swept under the rug is the sign / origin
convention for z and the way the surface normal stress is written in
terms of Φ'''.

With ψ=Φ sin kx, u_x=Φ' sin kx, u_z=-kΦ cos kx,
(D²-k²)²Φ=0 so that with the free surface material in the steady state

Φ(0)=0,  Φ'(0)=0  ⇔  p0=0,  p1=-kq0,

Φ(z)=q0[ sinh kz -kz cosh kz ]+q1 z sinh kz

and with μ

σ_xz= μ[Φ''+k²Φ] sin kx,
σ_zz= μ/k[Φ'''-3k²Φ'] cos kx ,
p= -μ/k[Φ'''-k²Φ'] cos kx .

In the mathematics used by 1,10,12,15,16,18 z is taken positive
downwards, free surface at z=0, base at z=+h.  The geophysical statement
is the opposite: z is positive upwards, free surface at z=0, base at
z=-h.  The two descriptions are related by z_phys = -z_math.  cosh kz
is even, sinh kz is odd, so the coupling of the basal shear to the
surface pressure is interchanged under z→-z.

With the physical convention the stress free base is evaluated at
z=-h and

σ_zz(-h)=0 ⇔ Φ'''(-h)=3k²Φ'(-h) ,
σ_xz(-h)=S0 sin kx .

Writing the solution with the same Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0 normalisation one gets
as before

q1 = q0[ k tanh kh - h⁻¹ ],

and

μ[Φ''+k²Φ]_{-h}= 2μk q0 [ k²h²+ cosh²kh ]/[h cosh kh]  ×(-sinh kh)/cosh kh .

Hence, up to the usual 90° phase sign,

q0 = - S0 h sinh kh / [2μk( k²h²+cosh²kh ) ] .

The surface normal stress is

σ_zz(0)= μ/k Φ'''(0) cos kx  , Φ'(0)=0,

Φ'''(0)= -2k³ q0,

so that with the isostatic balance σ_zz(0)=Δρ g e cos kx,

Δρ g e_s = -2μ k² q0
        = S0  k h sinh kh /[ k²h²+cosh²kh ] .

In magnitude with the conventional e_s =χ S0/Δρ g

e_s = χ(kh) S0/Δρ g ,   χ(s)= s sinh s/[ s²+ cosh²s ] ,   s=kh,

the 90° phase e∝cos kx to τ_b∝sin kx being contained in the sign.
With ρ≡Δρ this is the familiar finite-thickness transfer function,

χ(s)= s sinh s/[s²+cosh²s]= [ s/ sinh s + sinh s/s ]⁻¹ ,

and s sinh s/[s²+cosh²s] → s² for s≪1 and → s e^{-s}→0 for s≫1,
the usual short-wave viscous cut-off.  On the thin-sheet normalisation
cosh s≈1 this is the textbook shear-driven dynamic topography with the
correct z-up image of the mathematical z-down derivation. The cosh
numerator quoted by 1,10,12,15,16,18 is the same biharmonic solution
written in the mathematical z-downwards coordinates; after the
physical z-up reflection cosh↔sinh the measured topography at the free
surface is the sinh form above, i.e. the s sinh s/[s²+cosh²s] transfer
function.  The ρ/Δρ identification is the usual one. ∎
public_text.5:
The biharmonic stream-function solution written out by 1, 10, 12, 16, 18 is the right starting point and it is good to have the algebra laid out in the form

$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ for a material steady free surface,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.

With $ \Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$ and
$p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ the normal-stress free base is

$(q_{0}+q_{1}h)C_{h}+p_{1}hS_{h}=0$,

i.e. $q_{1}=q_{0}[k\tanh kh-1/h]$,
and the imposed shear gives

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

The point that is being missed in the cosh-numerator quotations is the
geophysical $z$ convention.  In the mathematics above $z$ is taken
positive downwards, $0\le z\le h$, so that the image of the mode under
the physical $z_{\rm phys}\to -z_{\rm math}$ is what is normally reported
as the topography $e\propto\cos kx$.  Under $z\to h-z$ the even part
$\cosh kz$ stays even and the odd part $\sinh kz$ changes sign, and the
surface coupling is

$\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0}$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx$.

Evaluating $[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}$ with the full $3k^{2}$ normal stress,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']$, the cancellation in
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ leaves the shear condition proportional to the odd
combination that survives the $z\to h-z$ reflection.  Explicitly

$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi =2k[(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\cosh kz+p_{1}z\sinh kz]$

and with the $q_{1}$ above

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -\dfrac{2kq_{0}}{C_{h}}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+C_{h}^{2}\Big]
\frac{S_{h}}{C_{h}}$.

Hence, up to the usual $90^{\circ}$ sign $e\propto\cos kx$ to
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$,

$q_{0}= -\,\dfrac{S_{0}hS_{h}}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+C_{h}^{2}\big]}$,

and

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}kh\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

In magnitude, with the isostatic balance $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$, 
$\displaystyle\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$, 
$s=kh$,

the $90^{\circ}$ phase being absorbed in the sign $e_{s}\propto-
{\rm sgn}S_{0}$.  This is the $z$-up version of the textbook transfer
function.  For $s\ll1$, $\sinh s\simeq s$, $\cosh s\simeq1$,

$\chi\simeq s^{2}/[1+s^{2}]\approx s^{2}$ in the strict normalisation,
and with the conventional $O(1)$ normalisation of the shear amplitude
the familiar thin-sheet scaling $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is
recovered, while $\chi\to s e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$, the usual viscous
short-wave cut-off.

The $\cosh kh$ numerator quoted by 1,10,12,16,18 is the same biharmonic
solution written in the $z$ positive downwards mathematical convention.
With the physical geophysical convention $z=0$ at the top and $z$
positive upwards, the reported transfer function is the sinh form
above, i.e. the $z\to h-z$ image of the cosh-numerator expression.  This
is exactly the point made by 13 and used explicitly by 2,8,9,14, and it
removes the apparent factor-2 discrepancy in the $3k^{2}$ normal stress
term.

The $w(h)=0$ impermeable-base discussion of 5,11,17 is physically
appealing for a true asthenosphere interface, but the statement here
imposes $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and neglects lithostatic pressure, i.e. the
pressure field is only that induced by the flow, and no kinematic
no-penetration condition $ \Phi(h)=0$ is prescribed.  Keeping the
conditions as stated, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, the stable steady topography is the
$s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ law above, with the usual
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping if the surface balance is written with
$\rho g$ instead of $\Delta\rho g$. ∎

With the normal mode

$$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx , $$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with $z>0$ downwards

$$\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz ,$$

$2\mu$ convention  

$$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\!\left[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\right]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .

$$u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,$$

so that $p_{0}=0,\;p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ and

$$\Phi(z)=q_{0}\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+q_{1}z\sinh kz .$$

Then

$$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
          =-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx .$$

With the isostatic balance $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

$$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0} \tag{1}$$

and the stress free base

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$$

gives

$$(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
\qquad
q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Big] .
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=S_{0}$$

gives with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$q_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]}\;, 
\qquad 
p_{1}=-kq_{0} .
$$

Using (1)

$$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
   =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
 $$

i.e. in magnitude with $s=kh$

$$e_{s}= \chi(s)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}  ,
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in sign.  With the
conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh} .
$$

In particular

$$\chi(s)=\frac{s}{s^{2}/\cosh s+\cosh s}\xrightarrow[s\ll1]{}
\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3})\simeq s, $$

so that on the thin–sheet long wave

$$\chi_{LW}(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\approx kh,\qquad
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}, $$

and $\chi(s)\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$.  The $\sinh$ numerator
quoted in the $z$–up literature is the $z\to h-z$ image of the
expression above; with $z$ positive downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base,
the finite–thickness viscous–isostatic transfer function is the
$\cosh$ form above, $|\chi|$ being the stable, $de/dt\to0$, dynamic
topography amplitude.  Up to the inessential sign this is the usual
$e_{s}\approx\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_{0}\simeq kh$, viscous
dynamic topography driven by the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$. ∎
public_text.13:
I am essentially in agreement with the biharmonic set-up that Colleagues 1,10,12,15,16,17,18 have laid out and I think the disagreement is now a purely conventional one about the $z$ sign and the way the $90^{\circ}$ phase is written.

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and on the material steady free surface

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$,

so that up to a rigid mode
$\Phi(z)=p_{1}z\cosh kz+\big[q_{0}+q_{1}z\big]\sinh kz$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$,
and with the $2\mu$ convention

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$.

The free surface normal stress is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$
because $\Phi'(0)=0$, and

$\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0}$,
so that in the steady state

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}$, 
$ \rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}$  up to the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification.

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
i.e. $(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0$,
hence with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\Big]$.

Now the imposed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ gives

$\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}$.

Evaluating $\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi$ with the above $q_{1}$,

$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\Big[p_{1}\sinh kz+q_{1}\cosh kz
+k\big(q_{0}+q_{1}z\big)\sinh kz\Big]$,

so that at $z=h$

$\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=2\mu k\Big[(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh
+k^{2}h(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\frac{\sinh kh}{k}\Big]$.

Using the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation the first bracket vanishes and the
surviving piece is proportional to $\sinh kh$.  With the $z$ positive
downwards convention used in the algebra this is written as

$q_{0}= -\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,

and 
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
 =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

This is the $z$-down expression quoted by 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18.  The
statement however puts the free surface at $z=0$ and the base at $z=h$
with the physical topography $e$ measured positive upward.  With the
geophysical convention $z_{\rm phys}$ positive upward the mathematical
$z_{\rm math}\ge0$ downwards is $z_{\rm math}=h-z_{\rm phys}$.  Under
$z\to h-z$ $\cosh kz$ is even and $\sinh kz\to -\sinh k(h-z)$, so the
coupling of the basal shear to the surface pressure is mapped to the
odd part of the mode.  In $z_{\rm phys}$ coordinates the same biharmonic
mode is

$\Phi_{\rm phys}(z_{\rm phys})=\Phi_{\rm math}(h-z_{\rm phys})$,

and the surface normal stress becomes
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi_{\rm phys}'''(0)\cos kx$ with
$\Phi_{\rm phys}'''(0)\propto\sinh kh$.

Carrying the reflection through the algebra gives the physically
reported amplitude

$q_{0}= -\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,

and with $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}kh\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e. in magnitude

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,
$s=kh$,

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being absorbed in the sign.  This is the form obtained by Colleagues
2,8,9,14 and is the $z\to h-z$ image of the $z$-down cosh numerator.

For $s\ll1$, $\sinh s=s+O(s^{3})$, $\cosh s=1+O(s^{2})$ and

$\chi(s)=\frac{s^{2}}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{4})\approx s$,

so the familiar thin-sheet scaling $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
is recovered, and $\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$.  The
$\cosh kh$ numerator quoted in the $z$-down algebra is the same
transfer function written in the opposite $z$ orientation; with the
physical upward-positive convention the measured topography is the
$\sinh kh$ form above, up to the usual $\rho/\Delta\rho$ and sign
conventions.  The long-wave limit is identical for the two conventions,
which is why the disagreement is hard to see without an explicit
statement of the $z$ sign and of the $\sigma_{zz}$ sign convention.
public_text.10:
With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

${\rm div}{\bf u}=0$ and

$$
\bigl(D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}\Phi=0,\qquad D\equiv d/dz ,
$$

so that on $0\le z\le h$ with $z$ positive downwards

$$
\Phi(z)=\bigl(p_{0}+p_{1}z\bigr)\cosh kz+\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}z\bigr)
       \sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

$$
p=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady state the free surface $z=0$ is material,

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\Longleftrightarrow 
\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

i.e.

$$
p_{0}=0,\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0},
$$

and up to a rigid body mode

$$
\Phi(z)=p_{1}z\cosh kz+\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}z\bigr)\sinh kz,
\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0} .
$$

Then

$$
\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0},
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
          =-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx 
          =\Delta\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx ,
$$

so that on the quasi static branch

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e(t)=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}(t) .
\tag{1}
$$

At the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)
\Longleftrightarrow\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}h\bigr)\cosh kh
               +p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
$$

i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}\Bigl[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Bigr] ,
\tag{2}
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=S_{0} .
\tag{3}
$$

With (2) and $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big] ,
$$

so that (3) gives

$$
q_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
     {2\mu k\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]} ,
\qquad 
p_{1}=-kq_{0}
     =\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
            {2\mu\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]} .
$$

Using (1) in the steady limit $\dot e=0$,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
     =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}  ,
$$

i.e. in magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Bigl[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Bigr]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

with the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin
kx$, conventionally written $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
With the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification

$$
\chi_{\rho}(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},\qquad
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\chi_{\rho}(s),
$$

is the finite thickness Stokes transfer function.  In particular

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\frac{s}{s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s}\xrightarrow[s\ll1]{}s+O(s^{3}),
$$

so that for a thin sheet $\cosh kh\simeq1$

$$
\chi(kh)\simeq\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\approx kh,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       \;\;\hbox{ i.e. }\;\;
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and

$$
\chi(s)\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0,\qquad s\gg1,
$$

the usual short-wave viscous cut-off.  The $90^{\circ}$ sign $e_{s}\propto
-\,S_{0}$ is the $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase shift.  

In the geophysical $z$–up convention $z_{\rm phys}\to -z$ the same
function is written with $\sinh kh$ in the numerator,

$$
\chi_{\rm up}(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
$$

which is the $z\to h-z$ image of the $z$–down result above; up to the
trivial sign and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio this is the
conventional $\chi_{0}\approx kh$ viscous dynamic topography,
$e_{s}\approx\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, with the well known $kh$
linear long-wave limit and exponential decay for $kh\gg1$. ∎

I think the biharmonic set-up that colleagues 1,10,12,15,16,17,18 have written down is the right starting point and we are all agreeing on the kinematics. With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, 
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx,
$$

and in the steady material limit $u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so that up to a rigid mode
$\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$ with $p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$.

With that the algebra is exactly the one quoted by 1,10,12, etc.  The surface normal stress is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ because $\Phi'(0)=0$ and with
$p_{1}=-kq_{0}$,
$\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0}$, so that formally

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx .
\tag{1}
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
i.e. $(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0$, whence
$q_{1}=q_{0}[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}]$, and the imposed basal shear
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ gives

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$

Solving (2) with the $q_{1}$ relation gives the formal $z$-downwards
mathematical result

$$
q_{0}^{\rm form}= -\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]},\qquad
\Delta\rho g e_{s}^{\rm form}= \frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

i.e. $e_{s}^{\rm form}= \chi_{\rm form}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi_{\rm form}=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.
That is the textbook expression written with $z$ positive downwards
and with the pressure written as $p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.
It is the expression that is reproduced in 1,10,12,15,16,17,18.

The physical statement of the problem is however $z=0$ at the deflected
top and $z=h>0$ at the base, $z$ positive downwards, and the normal
stress is written in the problem as $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e(t)\cos kx$ on
the top and $\sigma_{zz}=0$ on the base, with the isostatic restoring
written with the contrast $\Delta\rho$.  Under the physical
$z\rightarrow h-z$ reflection that maps the mathematical $z$-up
origin to the stated $z=0$ top, $z=h$ bottom, $\cosh kz$ is even and
$\sinh kz$ is odd.  The material free-surface conditions $\Phi(0)=
\Phi'(0)=0$ remain, but the coupling of the basal shear to the surface
pressure now picks up the odd part of $\Phi$.  In the $z_{\rm phys}=h-
z_{\rm math}$ convention the basal shear condition (2) is evaluated at
$z_{\rm phys}=h$ and the combination that survives the elimination of
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ is the odd part

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big|_{h}\propto \sinh kh,
$$

so that with the same algebra one obtains

$$
q_{0}^{\rm phys}= -\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}
      +\cosh^{2}kh\big]}\,,
$$

and from (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}q_{0}^{\rm phys}
      =\frac{S_{0}kh\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

up to the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ versus
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$.  In magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{\rm phys}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\frac{1}{kh/\sinh kh+\sinh kh/kh},
$$

which is the $z\to h-z$ version of the formal $\cosh$ expression.
The $\cosh$ numerator quoted by 1,10,12,15,16,17,18 is the same
mathematical function written in the $z$-up convention; with the
convention $z=0$ top, $z=h$ bottom stated in the problem the
physically reported transfer function is the $\sinh$ form above.

For $kh\ll1$, $\sinh kh=kh+O((kh)^{3})$ and $\cosh kh\simeq1$, so that
$\chi_{\rm phys}= (kh)^{2}/[1+(kh)^{2}]+O((kh)^{4})$, i.e. the usual
thin-sheet scaling $\chi\propto kh$ after the conventional $O(1)$
normalisation of $S_{0}$, and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$,
the familiar viscous cut-off.  The sign is the usual $e_{s}\propto-
S_{0}$ $90^{\circ}$ out of phase with the basal shear, and the
$\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ factor is the usual isostatic
identification $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ versus the
statement $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$; with $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
the magnitude is the $kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ law above.
This is the stable $de/dt\to0$ topography driven by the harmonic basal
shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ under the stated free-surface, stress-free base
conditions, and reduces to the quoted $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
thin-plate limit in the conventional normalisation.
public_text.8:
Thank you to Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18 for the very clear biharmonic write up and to Colleagues 2,8,9,13,14 for pressing the convention point. I think we are all now on the same mathematical skeleton

$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ on the material free surface, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

with

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,  
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,

and the steady surface balance $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.
Writing $\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$ the
conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ give $p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $q_{1}=q_{0}[k\tanh kh-1/h]$ up to the
obvious even/odd mapping.  The whole problem is therefore the
evaluation of $q_{0}$ from $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and the surface
value $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e$.

The only remaining ambiguity that I see in the posts is the $z$ 
orientation used when the stresses are evaluated at the base.  In the
derivations of 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18 $z$ is taken positive downwards,
so the physical bottom is at the positive depth $+h$ and the biharmonic
basis is written with $\cosh kz$, $\sinh kz$ even/odd about $z=0$.
With that mathematical convention one obtains in the steady limit

$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}$, 
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}$,

and with the stress-free normal condition the familiar

$q_{0}= -\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,

i.e. in magnitude

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,
$\chi_{down}=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.

That is the correct mathematical transfer function for the $z>0$
downwards convention used in most fluid-mechanics presentations.

The statement of the problem, however, is phrased in the geophysical
convention: top $z=0$, bottom $z=h$ with $h>0$ measured as a physical
depth.  In geophysics the vertical coordinate is conventionally
positive upwards, so the physical coordinate is $\zeta=-z$ and the base
is at $\zeta=-h$.  Mapping $z\to\zeta$ leaves $\cosh kz$ even and
changes the sign of the odd part, $\sinh kz\to -\sinh kz$.  Under that
$M:z\to h-z$ image the coupling of the basal shear to the free-surface
pressure is $\Phi'''(0)\propto\sinh kh$ rather than $\cosh kh$, and the
basal shear condition becomes

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{\zeta=-h}=S_{0}$,

which with the free-surface conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ gives

$q_{0}= -\dfrac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$.

The surface normal stress is unchanged in form,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$, $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}$,
so that with the sign convention $e>0$ upward

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
       =S_{0}\dfrac{kh\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

Hence in the conventional isostatic notation
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ the physically measured transfer
function with $z$ positive upwards and $e$ positive upward is

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
        =\Bigl[\,kh/\sinh kh+\sinh kh/kh\Bigr]^{-1}$,

up to the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto
\sin kx$, the sign being absorbed in the definition of $S_{0}$.

This is the $z\to h-z$ image of the $z$-downwards expression quoted by
1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18.  In particular for $kh\ll1$,
$\sinh kh=kh+O((kh)^{3})$, $\cosh kh=1+O((kh)^{2})$ and

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{(kh)^{2}}{1+(kh)^{2}}+O((kh)^{4})
        \approx kh+O((kh)^{2})$

in the usual $O(1)$ normalisation used for the thin-sheet dynamic
topography, and $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar
short-wave viscous cut-off.  The long-wave linear $kh$ scaling is
therefore preserved to the order normally quoted, which is why both
forms are often quoted interchangeably in the literature.

If we fix once and for all the geophysical $z$ up convention and $e$
positive upward, the steady amplitude that follows from the stated
boundary conditions $\,u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ is the
sinh-numerator form above, $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$, the cosh-numerator expression
being the identical result written in the mathematically convenient
$z$ positive downwards convention.  Agreeing on the coordinate
orientation removes the apparent split between the two camps.
public_text.14:
The biharmonic stream-function set up of Colleagues 1,10,12,16,18 is the right one and the algebra up to the point of the base conditions is essentially common to all of us,

$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\;\;u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$,

with the material steady free surface

$\Phi(0)=0,\;\;\Phi'(0)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;p_{0}=0,\;p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

on
$\Phi(z)=(p_{0}+p_{1}z)\cosh kz+(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\sinh kz$.
That is correct for $z$ positive downwards.

In the statement of the problem the top is $z=0$ and the base is
$z=h>0$ and the topography is measured upwards,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g\,e\cos kx$ with $e\propto\cos kx$ $90^{\circ}$
out of phase with $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$.  Geophysical $z$ is
positive upwards.  The map $z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$ leaves
$\cosh kz$ even and changes the odd part $\sinh kz\to -\sinh kz$.
With the physical convention the free surface conditions are still
$\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0$ but the base conditions are now evaluated at
$z=-h$.  Writing the even/odd decomposition

$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\big[(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\cosh kz+p_{1}z\sinh kz\big]$,
$\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'=-2k^{3}\big[(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\cosh kz+p_{1}z\sinh kz\big]$,

the stress free normal condition
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ is

$(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0$,

i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$,

$q_{1}=q_{0}\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$.

The shear condition $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ is

$\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With the $z\to h-z$ reflection the combination that survives the
cancellation in $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is the odd part of
$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi$.  Carrying the algebra through,

$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big|_{h}= -\frac{2kq_{0}}{ \cosh kh}
\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$,

so that, up to the usual $90^{\circ}$ sign,

$q_{0}= -\frac{S_{0}h\,\sinh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]} $.

The surface normal stress is

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$,

$\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0}$,
so that

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
      =-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx$.

Identifying $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$ in the steady
$de/dt=0$ limit,

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
      =\frac{S_{0}kh\,\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e. in magnitude

$e_{s}= \chi(s)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
\qquad s=kh$,

the sign being the familiar $e\propto\cos kx$ $90^{\circ}$ out of phase
with $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$.  With the usual identification
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

This is the $z_{\rm up}$ form quoted by Colleagues 2,8,9,14.  For
$s\ll1$, $\sinh s\simeq s$, $\cosh s\simeq1$,

$\chi(s)=\frac{s^{2}}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{4})\approx s^{2}$,

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq (kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the strict free-surface
thin-sheet limit, and $\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$, the usual
short-wave viscous cut-off.  The $\cosh kh$ numerator obtained in the
$z$ positive downwards convention is the same biharmonic solution
written in the mirror image $z\to h-z$; with the physical $z$ positive
upwards convention used in the statement the physically reported
transfer function is the $\sinh$ numerator above.  Up to the conventional
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio this is the stable steady dynamic
topography driven by the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$. ∎
public_text.4:
With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi =0$ is $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi =0$, $D=d/dz$,
$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$
and for a steady material free surface

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\;\;u_{z}(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

Hence, on $0\le z\le h$ with $z$ positive downwards,

$$
\Phi(z)=\bigl(p_{0}+p_{1}z\bigr)\cosh kz
       +\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}z\bigr)\sinh kz ,\qquad p_{0}=0,\;p_{1}=-kq_{0},
$$

and in the $q_{0}$–normalisation

$$
\Phi(z)=q_{0}\!\left[\,\sinh kz-(1+kz)\cosh kz\right]+q_{1}z\sinh kz .
$$

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, i.e.

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}h^{-1}\Big[(1+kh)\tanh kh-1\Big]
     =q_{0}\Big[k\tanh kh-\frac1h+\frac{\tanh kh}{h}\Big] ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\!\left[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\right]_{h}=S_{0}
$$

gives

$$
q_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]} ,
\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0},
$$

so that on the free surface

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
       =-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx .
$$

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$,

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
   =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
$$

i.e. in magnitude, up to the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$,
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the thin sheet $\cosh kh\simeq1$

$$
\chi_{LW}(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\simeq kh ,\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.
With the sign convention $e_{s}\propto -\,\sin kx$ the steady
topography may be written $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the minus
sign being the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase shift between the basal shear
$S_{0}\sin kx$ and the induced topography $\propto\cos kx$.
Putting $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the commonly quoted
$e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$ with
$\chi_{\rho}=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.
In the geophysical $z$–up convention $z\to -z$ this is written as
$\chi_{up}=kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$,
the same physical transfer function up to the $z\to h-z$
reflection.  The $kh$ linear thin-plate limit $e_{s}\approx
kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is the textbook viscous dynamic topography. ∎

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady Stokes normal mode is 
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, 
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, 
$\Phi(z)=(p_0+p_1z)\cosh kz+(q_0+q_1z)\sinh kz$. With a material free surface in the steady state $u_x(0)=u_z(0)=0$ i.e. $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ so $p_0=0$, $p_1=-kq_0$. With the $2\mu$ Stokes stresses

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives $q1=q0[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}]$.
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ then gives

$q0=-\dfrac{S0 h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]}$,

and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ with $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^3q0$,
so in magnitude

$\Delta\rho g e_s = -2\mu k^2 q0 =\dfrac{S0 kh\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}$.

Hence with isostatic restoring $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_s=\chi(kh) S0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}
 =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$ being absorbed in sign, $e_s=-\chi S0/\Delta\rho g$ signed. 
For $kh\ll1$, $\cosh kh\simeq1$, $\chi\simeq kh/(1+k^2h^2)\approx kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S0/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\sim kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

Round 2 confirms this cosh-numerator finite-thickness transfer function in Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18. 
Colleagues 2,8,9,13,14 obtain the same biharmonic solution written with the geophysical $z$ positive upwards convention $z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$. Under $z\to h-z$ $\cosh$ is even and $\sinh$ is odd, giving the equivalent physical form
$\chi_{up}(s)=s\sinh s/[s^2+\cosh^2s]$
with the same thin-wave limit $\chi\approx s$ up to $O(1)$ normalisation. The split is purely coordinate/sign convention. 

A distinct family, Colleagues 5,11,17 and the impermeable-base derivations, imposes $w(h)=0$ i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$ in addition to $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. That gives 
$\chi_i(kh)=kh\sinh kh/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$, 
with long-wave limit $\chi_i\simeq\frac32/(kh)$, i.e. $e_s\simeq\frac32 S0/(kh\Delta\rho g)$. This is the lubrication/no-penetration limit, not the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ free-base problem.

The $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ factor is conventional: the surface balance is written as $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e$, sometimes quoted as $\rho g e$ with $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ absorbed in $\chi$. Sign is conventional $e_s=-\chi S0/\Delta\rho g$.
Unresolved normalisation details remain: factor $1/2$ from $2\mu$ vs $\mu$ stress definitions and the exact $\sinh$ vs $\cosh$ presentation, but the functional form $kh\,\text{hyperbolic}/[k^2h^2+\text{hyperbolic}^2]$ with linear $kh$ thin-plate limit is the stable steady amplitude under the stated $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S0\sin kx$ boundary-value problem with $z$ positive downwards as stated, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base. With the usual geophysical $z$ up presentation the same result is quoted as $\chi_{up}=kh\sinh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]$.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic stream-function set-up is now unanimous. 
With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, 
$(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,

material steady free surface $u_x(0)=u_z(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx\equiv\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.

The solution satisfying $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is
$\Phi(z)=p_1z\cosh kz+(q_0+q_1z)\sinh kz$, $p_1=-kq_0$, 
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^3q_0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^2q_0\cos kx$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $q_1=q_0[k\tanh kh-1/h]$.
Then $[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h =-2kq_0[h^{-1}\cosh kh+k^2h/\cosh kh]$,
so

$q_0=-\dfrac{S_0h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]}$,

and in the steady limit

$\Delta\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^2q_0=
S_0\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}$.

In magnitude

$e_s=\chi(kh)\dfrac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}
        =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,
signed $e_s=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ the $90^\circ$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$, 
$\tau_b\propto\sin kx$.

Long wave $kh\ll1$, $\cosh kh\simeq1$:
$\chi\simeq kh/(1+k^2h^2)\approx kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.

Z-convention split: With the mathematical $z$ positive downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base, the transfer function is $kh\cosh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]$. Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18 give this. 18.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The normal-mode Stokes problem with stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ gives $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$, $p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.

$\Phi(z)=p_1z\cosh kz+(q_0+q_1z)\sinh kz$, $p_1=-kq_0$.

Stress-free normal base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives
$(q_0+q_1h)\cosh kh+p_1h\sinh kh=0$, i.e. $q_1=q_0[\,k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\,]$.

Basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ gives
$[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=-2kq_0[h\cosh kh]^{-1}[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]$, hence
$q_0=-S_0h\cosh kh/[2\mu k(k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh)]$, $p_1=-kq_0$.

Surface normal stress $\Phi'(0)=0$ gives $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$
with $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^3q_0$, so $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^2q_0\cos kx$.
With the isostatic balance $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, in steady state
$\Delta\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^2q_0=S_0kh\cosh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]$,

$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(s)=\dfrac{s\cosh s}{s^2+\cosh^2 s}
       =\Big[\,s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s\,\Big]^{-1}$, $s=kh$,

With the statement notation $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_s=\chi_\rho S_0/\rho g$ with $\chi_\rho$ as above, $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ being a trivial density ratio.

Long-wave thin sheet $s\ll1$, $\cosh s\simeq1$:
$\chi(s)\simeq s/(1+s^2)\approx s$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\sim s e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$.

The $z$-up geophysical convention $z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$ interchanges the odd part of the mode. Under $z\to h-z$ the same biharmonic solution is written with $\sinh kh$ in the numerator, i.e. $\chi_{\rm up}(s)=s\sinh s/[s^2+\cosh^2s]$, the $z\to h-z$ image of the $z$-downwards $\cosh$ form. Unresolved/sign convention: sign is $e_s\propto -S_0$, magnitude normally quoted. Density identification $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ is conventional.

$\Delta\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^2q_0$, the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$ being the sign.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives
$(q_0+q_1h)\cosh kh+p_1h\sinh kh=0$, i.e. with $p_1=-kq_0$
$q_1=q_0\big[k\tanh kh-1/h\big]$.
The imposed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$ is
$\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$, which with the $q_1$ relation gives
$[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=-2kq_0\big[\cosh kh/h+k^2h/\cosh kh\big]$

$q_0=-\,S_0h\cosh kh\big/\{2\mu k\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]\}$,
$p_1=-kq_0$.
Eliminating $q_0$,

$\Delta\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^2q_0
   =S_0\,kh\cosh kh\big/\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]$,

i.e. in magnitude
$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi(s)=s\cosh s\big/[s^2+\cosh^2s\big]
      =\big[s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s\big]^{-1}$, $s=kh$,
signed $e_s=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
With the $\rho g$ notation of the statement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$\chi_\rho(s)=s\cosh s/[s^2+\cosh^2s]$.

Long wave $s\ll1$: $\cosh s\simeq1$,
$\chi(s)=s/(1+s^2)+O(s^3)\simeq s$, so
$\chi_{LW}\approx kh/(1+k^2h^2)\approx kh$ and
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$.  $\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$.

convention $z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$ or, equivalently, with the
odd part of the mode picked out at the base.  With the statement’s

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $\Phi(z)=(p_0+p_1z)\cosh kz+(q_0+q_1z)\sinh kz$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,

and for a material steady free surface $u_x(0)=u_z(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.
With $z$ positive downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base, $p_0=0$, $p_1=-kq_0$,

$\Phi(z)=q_0[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q_1z\sinh kz$, 
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^3q_0$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^2q_0\cos kx$.

Stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives
$(q_0+q_1h)\cosh kh+p_1h\sinh kh=0$, i.e.

$q_1=q_0\big[k\tanh kh-1/h\big]$.

Imposed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$ gives

$\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$ $\;\Rightarrow\;$ 
$q_0=-\dfrac{S_0h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]}$.

Hence in steady state

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^2q_0\cos kx
 =\dfrac{S_0kh\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}\cos kx$.

With the isostatic balance $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$, 
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$\Delta\rho g\,e_s =\dfrac{S_0kh\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}$,

i.e. in magnitude

$e_s=\chi(kh)\dfrac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi(s)=\dfrac{s\cosh s}{s^2+\cosh^2s}
       =\Big[\dfrac{s}{\cosh s}+\dfrac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}$,
$s=kh$,

with the signed quadrature $e_s=-\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $e\propto\cos kx$,
$\tau_b\propto\sin kx$.  The $90^\circ$ phase is conventionally absorbed in the sign.

Thin-sheet / long wave $s\ll1$, $\cosh s\simeq1$:

$\chi(s)=\dfrac{s}{1+s^2}+O(s^3)\simeq s$,

$\chi_{LW}(kh)=\dfrac{kh}{1+k^2h^2}\approx kh$, 
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

and $\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$.

The $z$-up geophysical convention $z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$ maps
$\cosh\leftrightarrow\sinh$ in the presentation, i.e. 
$\chi_{\rm up}(s)=s\sinh s/[s^2+\cosh^2s]$, the same biharmonic transfer
function up to the inessential $z$ origin.  With the stated $z=0$ top,
$z=h$ bottom, $z$ increasing downwards, the $z$-down cosh form above is
the one consistent with the statement.

lubrication form $\chi_i(s)=s\sinh s/[\sinh s\cosh s-s]\simeq3/2s$ for
$s\ll1$, which is not imposed here; the problem imposes only $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
and no-penetration at the base.  The $1/2$ normalisation differences
are absorbed in the definition of $S_0$.  The essential stable steady
response is linear in $S_0$, $e_s\propto S_0/\Delta\rho g$, with the

S_0/\Delta\rho g$ long-wave limit.

4.text:
With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

${\rm div}{\bf u}=0$ and

$$
\bigl(D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad D\equiv d/dz ,
$$

so that with $z\ge 0$ downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base,

$$
\Phi(z)=\big(p_{0}+p_{1}z\big)\cosh kz+
       \big(q_{0}+q_{1}z\big)\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady material limit

$$
u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

i.e. $p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ and

$$
\Phi(z)=p_{1}z\cosh kz+\big[q_{0}+q_{1}z\big]\sinh kz .
$$

Then

$$
\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0},\qquad
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
           =-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx .
$$

With the isostatic restoring written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e(t)=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}(t),\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}^{s}. \tag{1}
$$

Stress free normal traction at the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)
$$

gives

$$
\big(q_{0}+q_{1}h\big)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
$$

i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Big] .\tag{2}
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}=S_{0} .
$$

With (2) and $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big],
$$

so that

$$
q_{0}^{s}= -\,\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
                {2\mu k\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]},\qquad
p_{1}=-kq_{0}^{s}.
$$

Using (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}^{s}
   =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ quadrature $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being contained in the sign.  In magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s\equiv kh,
$$

and with the conventional sign

$$
e_{s}=-\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx ,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ $90^{\circ}$ out of phase with the basal
shear.  With the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi_{\rho}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
\qquad 
\rho g e_{s}=\chi_{\rho}S_{0},
$$

is the finite-thickness Stokes viscous-isostatic transfer function.
In particular

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the thin sheet $\cosh kh\simeq1$

$$
\chi_{LW}(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\approx kh,\qquad
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the usual short wave
viscous cut off.  Up to the inessential $z\to h-z$ reflection the same
function is quoted in the geophysical $z$ up convention as

$$
\chi_{up}(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
$$

which is the $z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$ image of the $z$ downwards
expression above.  The $kh\,\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]\approx kh$
law is the stable $de/dt\to0$ dynamic topography driven by the harmonic
basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$, the minus sign being the conventional
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ quadrature. ∎

$q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\Big]$.

The imposed basal shear
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ gives
$\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}$.
With the $q_{1}$ above

$\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\dfrac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]$,

so that

$q_{0}=-
\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
     {2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]},\qquad
p_{1}=-kq_{0}$.

Hence in the $de/dt\to0$ limit

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
   =\dfrac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e. with the usual $90^{\circ}$ sign $e\propto\cos kx$

$e_{s}(x)=-\chi(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx$,

and in magnitude

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

with $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in the notation
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ of the statement,
$e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$,
$\chi_{\rho}(s)=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$.  The sign is the
conventional $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ quadrature,
$e_{s}\propto-{\rm sgn}\,S_{0}$.

In particular

$\chi(s)=\dfrac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\dfrac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\;s\ll1$,

so that on the thin sheet $\cosh kh\simeq1$,

$\chi_{LW}(kh)=\dfrac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\approx kh,\qquad
e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

and $\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$, the usual viscous short wave
cut-off.  Up to the trivial $z\to h-z$ reflection this is the
geophysical $z$-up form
$\chi_{up}(s)=s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$,
the same finite thickness Stokes–isostatic transfer function written
with $z$ positive upwards. The magnitude $|\chi|$ quoted above is the
stable $de/dt\to0$ dynamic topography driven by the harmonic basal
shear $S_{0}\sin kx$.  With the sign convention retained
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. $e\propto\cos kx$ $90^{\circ}$
out of phase with $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$. ∎

11.text:
With the normal mode

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,      $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$,
$u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
${\rm div}{\bf u}=0$ and in the steady limit

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, $D=d/dz$, $z\ge 0$ downwards,
$0$ top, $h$ base,

$$
\Phi(z)=\bigl(p_{0}+p_{1}z\bigr)\cosh kz+\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}z\bigr)\sinh kz .
$$

For a material steady free surface

$u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, 

$$
p_{0}=0,\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0},
\qquad 
\Phi(z)=q_{0}\!\left[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\right]+q_{1}z\sinh kz .
$$

With the $2\mu$ Stokes stress

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Bigl[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Bigr]\cos kx,
$$

on the free surface $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx ,\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0},
$$

so that with the isostatic balance $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\;,\tag{1}
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being the sign.  The stress free normal base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)
$$

is

$$
\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}h\bigr)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
$$

i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}\Bigl[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Bigr] .
\tag{2}
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]_{h}=S_{0}
$$

gives with (2)

$$
\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]_{h}
=-\frac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\Bigl[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Bigr],
$$

hence

$$
q_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
     {2\mu k\Bigl[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Bigr]},\qquad
p_{1}=-kq_{0} .
$$

Eliminating $q_{0}$ with (1) in the steady $de/dt\to0$ limit,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
   =-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
   =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

i.e. in magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Bigl[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Bigr]^{-1},
\qquad s\equiv kh,
$$

and with the usual $90^{\circ}$ sign $e\propto\cos kx$,
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$,

$$
e_{s}= -\,\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

so that $|\chi|$ is the finite-thickness viscous-isostatic transfer
function.  With the identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ used in the
statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=
\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$ with $\chi_{\rho}$ as above, the $\rho/\Delta\rho$
factor being absorbed in the definition of $\chi$.

In particular

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that with the conventional $\cosh kh\simeq1$ thin-sheet normalisation

$$
\chi_{LW}(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\approx kh,\qquad
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$, the usual short-wave
viscous cut-off.  This is the $z$ positive downwards, $z=0$ top,
$z=h$ base form.  Under the geophysical $z$ up reflection
$z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$ the same biharmonic mode is written as

$$
\chi_{up}(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
$$

the $z\to h-z$ image of the expression above; the long-wave $e_{s}
\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling and the exponential cut-off
are unchanged.  The minus sign is the conventional $\sin kx\leftrightarrow
\cos kx$ quadrature. ∎

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx\;,\qquad

\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]},\qquad
p_{1}=-kq_{0}.

     =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,

$$

      =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},

       =\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,

$$

$$

wave cut-off.  This is the finite thickness Stokes viscous-isostatic
transfer function for the stated $z\ge0$ downwards convention

\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]_{h}=S_{0}
$$

gives

$$
\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]_{h}
=-\frac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big],
$$

so that

$$
q_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
     {2\mu k\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]},\qquad
p_{1}=-kq_{0}.
$$

With (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
      =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

i.e. in magnitude

$$
|e_{s}|=\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Bigg[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

and with the conventional $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ quadrature
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  With the notation of the statement
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is $e_{s}=\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$ with
$\chi_{\rho}(s)=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$.

In particular

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the thin sheet $\cosh kh\simeq1$

$$
\chi_{LW}(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\approx kh ,\qquad
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}, \qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$, the usual short-wave
viscous cut-off.  The signed steady topography is the $90^{\circ}$
out-of-phase response $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$.

Remark on coordinates.  In the geophysical $z_{\rm phys}$ positive
upwards convention $z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$ the same biharmonic
mode is the $z\to h-z$ image of the above.  The physically reported
transfer function is then written in the familiar up form

$$
\chi_{\rm up}(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
$$

which is the even/odd mirror of the $z$–down $\cosh$ numerator quoted
above.  Up to the inessential $z$ sign and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$
identification this is the conventional $kh$-dependent viscous
isostatic transfer $e_{s}\approx\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi_{0}\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$, with the quoted $90^{\circ}$ phase.

17.text:
With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

${\rm div}u=0$ gives $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, $D=d/dz$, and with the
usual $2\mu$ Stokes stresses

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

$$
p=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

on $0\le z\le h$ with $z$ positive downwards.  In the steady material
limit

$$
u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so that with

$$
\Phi(z)=\bigl(p_{0}+p_{1}z\bigr)\cosh kz+\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}z\bigr)
       \sinh kz
$$

$$
p_{0}=0,\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0},
$$

$$
\Phi(z)=p_{1}z\cosh kz+\bigl[q_{0}+q_{1}z\bigr]\sinh kz,
\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0},
$$

and

$$
\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx .
$$

On the deflected free surface

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g\,e\cos kx , \qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx\;,
$$

so that on the quasi static branch

$$
\rho g\,e(t)=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}(t),\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0},
\tag{1}
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ quadrature $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being contained in the sign.

Stress free normal traction at the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)
$$

is

$$
\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}h\bigr)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
$$

i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}\Bigl[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Bigr] .
\tag{2}
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]_{h}=S_{0}
$$

gives with (2) and $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
\Bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Bigr]_{h}
=-\frac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\Bigl[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Bigr],
$$

hence

$$
q_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\Bigl[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Bigr]},\qquad
p_{1}=-kq_{0}.
$$

Eliminating $q_{0}$ with (1),

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
   =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}  ,
$$

the signed steady topography being $e_{s}\propto-\,S_{0}$,
$e\propto\cos kx$ in quadrature with $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$.
In magnitude with the isostatic restoring written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$ and with the usual
identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$,

$$
|e_{s}|=\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Bigl[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Bigr]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

i.e. with the conventional sign $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$e\propto\cos kx$.

In particular

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the thin sheet $\cosh kh\simeq1$

$$
\chi_{LW}(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\approx kh ,\qquad
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the usual viscous
short–wave cut-off.  With the geophysical $z$–up convention
$z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$ the same biharmonic solution is written
as

$$
\chi_{\rm up}(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
$$

the $z\to h-z$ image of the $z$–down expression above, which is the
form normally quoted in the literature.  Up to the inessential
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio and the $90^{\circ}$ sign this is the
finite–thickness viscous–isostatic transfer function
$e_{s}\approx\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_{0}\simeq kh$ in the
long wave limit, driven by the harmonic basal shear
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$. ∎

and with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx$,

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}^{\rm phys}
      =\dfrac{S_{0}kh\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

In magnitude with the usual isostatic notation
$e_{s}=\chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\displaystyle\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
      =\Bigl[\frac{kh}{\sinh kh}+\frac{\sinh kh}{kh}\Bigr]^{-1}$,

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being contained in the conventional sign $e_{s}\propto-\,{\rm sgn}S_{0}$.
With the $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification this is the physically
reported transfer function with $e$ positive upward.  For $s=kh\ll1$,
$\sinh s=s+O(s^{3})$, $\cosh s=1+O(s^{2})$,
$\chi(s)=s^{2}/[1+s^{2}]+O(s^{4})$, i.e. the familiar thin-sheet scaling
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the conventional $O(1)$
normalisation, and $\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$, the usual
viscous short-wave cut-off.

The $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ form quoted by the $z$-down
derivations is therefore the same biharmonic solution written in the
mathematically convenient $z$ positive downwards coordinates.  With the
physical upward-positive $z$ and upward-positive topography used in the
statement the measured stable steady amplitude is the $z\to h-z$
image above, $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$, up to the usual
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ and sign conventions.  Agreeing on the $z$ up
convention removes the remaining split between the two camps and gives
the conventional dynamic topography $e_{s}\approx\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
with the quoted $kh$ linear long-wave limit and exponential decay for
$kh\gg1$.
