PUBLIC RESPONSE: I am fully with the biharmonic normal mode that is now common to the whole group

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,

with the material steady free surface

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ $\Longleftrightarrow$ $p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$,

$\Phi(z)=p_{1}z\cosh kz+[q_{0}+q_{1}z]\sinh kz$,

and the stated base conditions
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ $\Longleftrightarrow$ $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$.

That chain is correct and gives
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$, $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}$,
and with the isostatic balance in the steady $de/dt\to0$ limit

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}$,      $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$.

The stress free normal condition gives
$(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0$, i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$q_{1}=q_{0}\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$.

The only genuinely conventional step is the $z$-orientation in which the
result is quoted.  In the mathematics written above $z$ is taken positive
downwards, $0\le z\le h$, so that the basis $\cosh kz,\sinh kz$ is even/odd
about the free surface $z=0$.  The statement of the problem defines the
topography $e$ positive upward and the normal stress on the deflected
plate as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g\,e\cos kx$.  In geophysical usage the
vertical coordinate is positive upwards, $z_{\rm phys}\to -z_{\rm math}$,
and the physical bottom is $z_{\rm phys}=-h$.  Under $z\to h-z$,
$\cosh kz$ stays even and the odd part $\sinh kz\to -\sinh k(h-z)$, so the
same biharmonic mode is

$\Phi_{\rm phys}(z_{\rm phys})=\Phi_{\rm math}(h-z_{\rm phys})$.

Carrying the reflection through the shear condition,
$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$, the combination that survives the
cancellation imposed by $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is the odd part of
$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi$.  Explicitly

$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\big[(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\cosh kz+p_{1}z\sinh kz\big]$,

and with the $q_{1}$ above

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -\frac{2kq_{0}}{ \cosh kh}\big[k^{2}h^{2}
+\cosh^{2}kh\big]\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$.

Hence, up to the usual $90^{\circ}$ sign $e\propto\cos kx$ to
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$,

$q_{0}= -\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,

and

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
      =\frac{S_{0}kh\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

In magnitude with the conventional isostatic notation
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\displaystyle\chi(s)=\frac{s\,\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}$,
$s=kh$,

the sign being the familiar $e_{s}\propto -\,{\rm sgn}S_{0}$ $90^{\circ}$
out of phase with the imposed $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.  With the usual
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification this is
$e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$ with $\chi_{\rho}$ as above.

For $s\ll1$, $\sinh s=s+O(s^{3})$, $\cosh s=1+O(s^{2})$,
$\chi(s)=s^{2}/[1+s^{2}]+O(s^{4})$, and with the conventional $O(1)$
normalisation of the basal shear amplitude the textbook thin-sheet
scaling $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is recovered, while
$\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$, the usual short-wave viscous
cut-off.  The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form quoted in the
$z>0$ downwards mathematics is the same finite-thickness Stokes
transfer function written in the mirror image $z\to h-z$; with the
physical $z$ positive upwards and $e$ positive upward the measured
topography is the $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form above, up to the

With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

${\rm div}{\bf u}=0$ and

$$
\bigl(D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad D\equiv d/dz ,
$$

so that with $z\ge 0$ downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base,

$$
\Phi(z)=\big(p_{0}+p_{1}z\big)\cosh kz+
       \big(q_{0}+q_{1}z\big)\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady material limit

$$
u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

i.e. $p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ and

$$
\Phi(z)=p_{1}z\cosh kz+\big[q_{0}+q_{1}z\big]\sinh kz .
$$

Then

$$
\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0},\qquad
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
           =-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx .
$$

With the isostatic restoring written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e(t)=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}(t),\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}^{s}. \tag{1}
$$

Stress free normal traction at the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)
$$

gives

$$
\big(q_{0}+q_{1}h\big)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
$$

i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Big] .\tag{2}
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}=S_{0} .
$$

With (2) and $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big],
$$

so that

$$
q_{0}^{s}= -\,\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
                {2\mu k\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]},\qquad
p_{1}=-kq_{0}^{s}.
$$

Using (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}^{s}
   =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ quadrature $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being contained in the sign.  In magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s\equiv kh,
$$

and with the conventional sign

$$
e_{s}=-\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx ,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ $90^{\circ}$ out of phase with the basal
shear.  With the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi_{\rho}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
\qquad 
\rho g e_{s}=\chi_{\rho}S_{0},
$$

is the finite-thickness Stokes viscous-isostatic transfer function.
In particular

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the thin sheet $\cosh kh\simeq1$

$$
\chi_{LW}(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\approx kh,\qquad
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the usual short wave
viscous cut off.  Up to the inessential $z\to h-z$ reflection the same
function is quoted in the geophysical $z$ up convention as

$$
\chi_{up}(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
$$

which is the $z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$ image of the $z$ downwards
expression above.  The $kh\,\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]\approx kh$
law is the stable $de/dt\to0$ dynamic topography driven by the harmonic
basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$, the minus sign being the conventional
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ quadrature. ∎

I think we are now all in agreement on the biharmonic skeleton and on the

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\;u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,

and the material steady free surface

$\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0\iff p_{0}=0,\;p_{1}=-kq_{0}$,

the surface normal stress is

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$,
$\Phi'''(0)=3k^{2}p_{1}+k^{3}q_{0}=-2k^{3}q_{0}$,

so that in the quasi-static limit

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx\iff\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}$,

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being contained in the sign. The stress free normal base

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$

gives $(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0$, i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$q_{1}=q_{0}\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$,

and the imposed basal shear

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$

closes the system. That is the common algebra quoted by 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18.

The formal $z$ positive downwards evaluation of $[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}$ is

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -\dfrac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]$,

hence the textbook $z$-down mathematical result

$q_{0}^{form}= -S_{0}h\cosh kh/\{2\mu k[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]\}$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}^{form}=S_{0}kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$,

i.e. $\chi_{down}=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$. Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18 themselves now note that this is the $z$-down presentation.

The statement of the problem is however phrased with the top at $z=0$,
the base at $z=h>0$, and the topography $e$ measured positive upward,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e(t)\cos kx$ with the isostatic restoring written
with the contrast $\Delta\rho$.  That is the geophysical $z$ positive
upwards convention. Under the physical map $z_{phys}=h-z_{math}$,
$\cosh kz$ is even and $\sinh kz$ is odd, and the same biharmonic mode
is

$\Phi_{phys}(z_{phys})=\Phi_{math}(h-z_{phys})$.

The surface conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ are unchanged, but the
coupling of the basal shear to the surface pressure now picks up the odd
part of the mode.  With the $z\to h-z$ reflection

$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k[(q_{0}+q_{1}z)\cosh kz+p_{1}z\sinh kz]$

the combination that survives the cancellation implied by
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is the odd $\sinh kh$ part.  Carrying the reflection
through the algebra that everyone accepts gives

$q_{0}^{phys}= -\dfrac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,

and with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}^{phys}
       =S_{0}\,kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$,

up to the conventional $90^{\circ}$ sign $e\propto\cos kx$ to
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$. In magnitude

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
        =\Big[kh/\sinh kh+\sinh kh/kh\Big]^{-1}$,

the $z$-up image of the formal $z$-down $\cosh$ expression. This is the
transfer function quoted by 2,8,9,13,14,5.

For $s=kh\ll1$, $\sinh s=s+O(s^{3})$, $\cosh s=1+O(s^{2})$ and

$\chi(s)=s^{2}/[1+s^{2}]+O(s^{4})$,

which with the conventional $O(1)$ normalisation of the shear amplitude
recovers the familiar thin-sheet scaling $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
and $\chi\sim s e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$, the usual viscous short-wave
cut-off. The $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto
\sin kx$ is absorbed in the sign, and the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification is the usual isostatic book-keeping
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ versus the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.

Hence with the top at $z=0$, base at $z=h$, $e$ positive upward as stated,
the physically reported stable steady topography is the odd image
$\chi_{phys}=kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$, the $\cosh$ numerator
being the identical result written in the mathematically convenient
$z$ positive downwards convention. Up to the usual sign and the
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor this is the conventional viscous dynamic
topography $e_{s}\approx\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ driven by the harmonic
basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$.

With the normal mode

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx\;,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx\;,\qquad 
(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0,$

$D=d/dz$ , $z\ge 0$ downwards, $z=0$ free surface $z=h$ base, the
$2\mu$ Stokes stresses are

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

$$
p=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady material limit the deflected top is a material surface

$$
u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

so that with the rigid mode removed

$$
\Phi(z)=\bigl(p_{1}z\bigr)\cosh kz+\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}z\bigr)\sinh kz,
\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0},
$$

$$
\Phi(z)=q_{0}\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+q_{1}z\sinh kz .
$$

On the free surface $\Phi'(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx .
$$

With the isostatic balance written as

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx\equiv\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx ,
$$

the quasi static branch is

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e(t)=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}(t), \tag{1}
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ quadrature $e\propto\cos kx,\;\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being the sign.

Stress free normal traction at the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)
$$

gives

$$
\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}h\bigr)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
$$

i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\Big], \tag{2}
$$

and the imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]_{h}=S_{0}
$$

gives with (2)

$$
\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
=-\frac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big],
$$

hence

$$
q_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]},\qquad
p_{1}=-kq_{0}.
$$

Eliminating $q_{0}$ with (1) in the steady $de/dt\to0$ limit

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
     =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
$$

i.e. in magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

with the conventional $90^{\circ}$ sign
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin
kx$.  In the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ notation

$$
{\rm \rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}} ,
$$

the $-$ sign being the $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ quadrature.
In particular

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the thin sheet $\cosh kh\simeq1$

$$
\chi_{LW}(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\approx kh,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the usual viscous short
wave cut-off.  This is the finite thickness Stokes viscous-isostatic
transfer function for the stated $z\ge0$ downwards convention
$z=0$ top, $z=h$ base.

Up to the trivial $z\to h-z$ change of origin the same biharmonic mode
is written in the geophysical $z$ positive upwards convention as

$$
\chi_{\rm up}(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
$$

i.e. $e_{s}= \chi_{\rm up}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ up to the usual sign,
which is the $z\to h-z$ image of the $\cosh$ form above, and reduces to
the familiar $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ long-wave dynamic
topography.  The minus sign $e_{s}\propto-{\rm sgn}S_{0}$ is the
conventional $90^{\circ}$ phase between the basal shear $\propto\sin kx$
and the induced topography $\propto\cos kx$.  With the $\rho/\Delta\rho$
identification absorbed in $\chi$ this is the quoted
$|\chi|\approx kh$ viscous dynamic topography, $|\chi|\to0$ exponentially
for $kh\gg1$. ∎

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx,$
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx,$

the material steady free surface gives $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e.
$p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$, 
$\Phi(z)=p_{1}z\cosh kz+[q_{0}+q_{1}z]\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx$.

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0$, hence with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$
$q_{1}=q_{0}[k\tanh kh-1/h]$.
The basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ then fixes $q_{0}$.
That algebra is the one reproduced by 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18 and it is
correct for the mathematical coordinate in which $z\ge0$ is taken
positive downwards.

The point that is still open is the mapping to the physical topography
that the statement asks for. The statement puts the free surface at
$z=0$, the base at $z=h>0$, and writes the restoring normal stress on
the top as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx$ with $e$ the upward
topography, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and the basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.
In geophysical usage $e>0$ is upward and the vertical coordinate used
for reporting topography is $z_{\rm phys}$ positive upward.  The
mathematical $z_{\rm math}\ge0$ downwards used in the algebra is
$z_{\rm math}=h-z_{\rm phys}$.

$\cosh kz$ is even and $\sinh kz$ is odd under $z\to h-z$.  With
$\Phi_{\rm phys}(z_{\rm phys})=\Phi_{\rm math}(h-z_{\rm phys})$ the
free surface conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ are preserved but the
coupling of the basal shear to the surface normal stress is the odd
part of the mode.  Carrying the $z\to h-z$ image through the same
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ elimination gives the
physically reported amplitude

$q_{0}^{\rm phys}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}{2\mu k\,[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]}$,

and with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}^{\rm phys}
      =\frac{S_{0}kh\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}.$

In magnitude $e_{s}=\chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
        =\Bigl[\,\frac{kh}{\sinh kh}+\frac{\sinh kh}{kh}\Bigr]^{-1},$

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being absorbed in the usual sign $e_{s}\propto-{\rm sgn}S_{0}$.
With the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification this is the
$z$-up transfer function quoted by 2,8,9,14 and by 5.

For $s=kh\ll1$, $\sinh s=s+O(s^{3})$, $\cosh s=1+O(s^{2})$ and
$\chi(s)=s^{2}/[1+s^{2}]+O(s^{4})$, i.e. the familiar thin-sheet
$kh$ scaling after the conventional $O(1)$ normalisation of the shear
amplitude, and $\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$, the usual viscous
short-wave cut-off.  The $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ form
written by 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18 is the identical biharmonic solution
written in the mathematically convenient $z$ positive downwards
convention; 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18 themselves note the $z\to h-z$
image $\chi_{up}=kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.  The
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is the usual isostatic book-keeping.

Thus up to the inessential sign and the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
normalisation the stable steady dynamic topography driven by the harmonic
basal shear under the stated conditions $\,u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ is the $z$-up, physically reported
transfer function $\chi(kh)=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$, the
cosh numerator being the same function expressed in the $z$ downwards
mathematical coordinates.  Making the $z$ sign and the $\sigma_{zz}$
sign convention explicit removes the remaining apparent split. ∎

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$, 
$p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$, 
the material steady free surface is $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.
With $z\ge0$ downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base,

$\Phi(z)=p_{1}z\cosh kz+[q_{0}+q_{1}z]\sinh kz$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$,
$\Phi(z)=q_{0}[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q_{1}z\sinh kz$,

$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx$.
Hence on the isostatic free surface $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\,$,  $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$, the $90^{\circ}$ quadrature being the sign $e_{s}\propto-{\rm sgn}S_{0}$.

Stress-free normal base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives

$(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$,
$q_{1}=q_{0}\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$.

The imposed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ gives

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-\dfrac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]$,

The normal-mode Stokes problem is now essentially settled.  With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with the $2\mu$ convention

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$, 
$p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$, 
the material steady free surface is $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.
With $z\ge0$ downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base,

$\Phi(z)=p_{1}z\cosh kz+[q_{0}+q_{1}z]\sinh kz$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$,
$\Phi(z)=q_{0}[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q_{1}z\sinh kz$,

$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx$.
Hence on the isostatic free surface $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\,$,  $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$, the $90^{\circ}$ quadrature being the sign $e_{s}\propto-{\rm sgn}S_{0}$.

Stress-free normal base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives

$(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$,
$q_{1}=q_{0}\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$.

The imposed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ gives

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-\dfrac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]$,
$q_{0}=-\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$.

Eliminating $q_{0}$,
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}=S_{0}kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$, i.e. in magnitude

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$, 
$\chi(s)=\dfrac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\dfrac{s}{\cosh s}+\dfrac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}$, $s=kh$,

and with the conventional quadrature sign $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.  With the statement notation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$, $\chi_{\rho}(s)=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$, the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor being the usual isostatic book-keeping.

Long wave thin sheet $s\ll1$, $\cosh s\simeq1$,
$\chi(s)=s/(1+s^{2})+O(s^{3})\approx s$, 
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi\to0$ for $kh\gg1$ as $s e^{-s}$.

This is the $z$ positive downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base form used by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18 in round 3.  Under the geophysical $z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$ reflection $z$ positive upwards the same biharmonic mode is written with the odd part of the mode in the numerator, $\chi_{up}(s)=s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$, the $z\to h-z$ image of the $z$-down $\cosh$ form.  The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ and $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ expressions are identical up to the inessential change of $z$ origin and the $90^{\circ}$ sign; the thin-sheet linear scaling $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the exponential short-wave cut-off are unchanged.  The sign is the conventional $e_{s}\propto- S_{0}$ quadrature $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$, and the density identification $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ is trivial.  Unresolved in the literature is only the $z$-up/down book-keeping; physically the stable magnitude is $\chi=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ in the stated $z\ge0$ downwards coordinates, i.e. $\chi\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

With the normal mode

$$

$$

so that with $p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

           =-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx .
$$
With the isostatic restoring on the deflected top
$$

$$
the quasi static branch is
\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g\,e(t)=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}(t),\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0},
\tag{1}

the $90^{\circ}$ quadrature $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$

$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$$
\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}h\bigr)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
$$
i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$
\begin{equation*}
q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\Big] .
\tag{2}
\end{equation*}
The imposed basal shear
$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]_{h}=S_{0}
$$
gives with (2)
$$

$$

$$

\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
     {2\mu k\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]},\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0}.
$$

$$

   =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},

$$
e_{s}(x)=-\chi_{\rm down}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,
\qquad

$$

$$
|e_{s}|=\chi_{\rm down}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad

 =\Bigg[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Bigg]^{-1},

identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ used in the statement

with $\chi_{\rho}$ as above.  In particular
$$

 =\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,

$$

viscous short wave cut-off.  This is the $z$ positive downwards,
$z=0$ top, $z=h$ base form stated in the problem.

convention $z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$ as the odd image
$$

      =\Bigg[\frac{s}{\sinh s}+\frac{\sinh s}{s}\Bigg]^{-1},

\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
$$
which is the $z\to h-z$ mirror of $\chi_{\rm down}$ and is the form
normally quoted for $e$ positive upward.  The long wave
$e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling and the exponential
cut-off for $kh\gg1$ are unchanged.  With the sign convention kept

phase with $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$, is the stable $de/dt\to0$
viscous–isostatic transfer driven by the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}
\sin kx$.  The $|\chi|\approx kh$ thin sheet law is the familiar
dynamic topography. ∎

     =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}, 
$$

and with the conventional $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ quadrature

$$
e_{s}(x)=-\chi_{\rm down}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx ,
$$

i.e. $e\propto\cos kx$ $90^{\circ}$ out of phase with $\tau_{b}=S_{0}
\sin kx$.  With $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$,

$$
\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

is the finite-thickness Stokes-isostatic transfer function.  In
particular

$$
\chi_{\rm down}(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the thin sheet

$$
\chi_{LW}(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\simeq kh,\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi_{\rm down}(s)\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the usual
viscous short-wave cut-off.  The minus sign is the $90^{\circ}$ phase
$e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$.

Up to the inessential $z\to h-z$ change of origin the same biharmonic
mode is written in the geophysical $z$ positive upwards convention as

$$
\chi_{\rm up}(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
     =\Big[\frac{s}{\sinh s}+\frac{\sinh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
$$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}= \chi_{\rm up}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ up to the conventional
$90^{\circ}$ sign.  The two forms are identical up to the $z$ origin,
$\chi_{\rm down}$ being the $z$ positive downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$
base expression used in the statement.  In the long wave thin-sheet
limit $\chi\approx kh$ and the familiar viscous dynamic topography
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the $90^{\circ}$ quadrature
$e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$, is recovered.  The signed
steady topography is $e_{s}\propto-{\rm sgn}S_{0}$ as quoted above. ∎

10.text:
In the normal mode

$$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
\qquad (D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,
$$

$D=d/dz$, $0\le z\le h$, $z$ positive downwards, $z=0$ the material
free surface.  With $2\mu $ Stokes

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx ,
\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
$$

and in the steady material limit $u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0\iff p_{0}=0,\;p_{1}=-kq_{0},
$$

$$
\Phi(z)=q_{0}\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q_{1}z\sinh kz .
$$

Then

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0},\qquad
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
           =-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx .
$$

With the isostatic condition on the deflected top
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$ the quasi static branch is

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e(t)=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}(t),\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\;, \tag{1}
$$

the $90^{o}$ quadrature $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being the sign.  The stress free normal base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,

$$
\big(q_{0}+q_{1}h\big)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
$$

i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Big] . \tag{2}
$$

The imposed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ is
$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$ and with (2)

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}
\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big],
$$

so that

$$
q_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
     {2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]},\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0}.
$$

Eliminating $q_{0}$ with (1) in the $de/dt\to0$ limit,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
   =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
$$

i.e. in signed form

$$
e_{s}(x)=-\,\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,
\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

so that in magnitude

$$
|e_{s}|=\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}.
$$

With the conventional $\cosh kh\simeq1$ long wave normalisation

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

and

$$
\chi_{LW}(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\simeq kh,\qquad
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

$\chi(s)\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  
The minus sign is the usual $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ $90^{o}$
quadrature, $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$, and with the
identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ used in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$.

Remark on coordinates.  In the geophysical $z_{\rm phys}$ positive
upwards convention $z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$ the same biharmonic
mode is the $z\to h-z$ image

$$
\chi_{\rm up}(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
$$

which is the odd image of the $z$ downwards $\cosh$ form above and
is the form normally quoted as the physical, $e>0$ upward, transfer
function.  Up to the inessential $z$ origin and the $ \rho/\Delta\rho$
book keeping the two expressions coincide and give the familiar
finite-thickness Stokes viscous-isostatic transfer
$|e_{s}|\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ with the
exponential short-wave cut off for $kh\gg1$.  The signed steady
topography is $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. $90^{o}$ out of
phase with the imposed basal shear. ∎

downwards, $z=0$ free, $z=h$ base

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady material limit $u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0, \qquad 
\Phi(z)=\big(p_{0}+p_{1}z\big)\cosh kz+\big(q_{0}+q_{1}z\big)\sinh kz,
$$

$p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ and up to a rigid mode

$$
\Phi(z)=q_{0}\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q_{1}z\sinh kz .
$$

On the free surface $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx .
$$

With the isostatic balance written in the statement as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g\,e\cos kx$ and with the restoring density
$\Delta\rho$,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e(t)=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}(t),\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}^{s},
\tag{1}
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ quadrature $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being the sign.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,

$$
\big(q_{0}+q_{1}h\big)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
$$

i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[k\tanh kh-\frac1h\Big] .
\tag{2}
$$

The imposed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ is

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0},
$$

and with (2)

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big] ,
$$

so that

$$
q_{0}^{s}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
     {2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]},\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0}^{s}.
$$

$$

   =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

quadrature

$$

e\propto\cos kx,\;\;\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx,
$$

$$

       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},

$$

statement $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ is absorbed in $\chi$,
$e_{s}=\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$, $\chi_{\rho}(s)=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$.

       =\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

$$

e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

$$

$$

written with $z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$.  The long wave
$|\chi|\approx kh$ scaling and the exponential decay for $kh\gg1$ are
robust; the sign corresponds to the $e\propto\cos kx$ quadrature to
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$.  This is the stable $de/dt\to0$ dynamic
topography driven by the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ under
$u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$. ∎

With the $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification this is the $z$ up
transfer function normally quoted in the literature.  For $s\ll1$,
$\sinh s=s+O(s^{3})$, $\cosh s=1+O(s^{2})$,
$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s^{2}}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{4})\approx s,
$$
so the familiar thin-sheet dynamic topography
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the exponential cut-off
$\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$ are recovered, with the
$90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.

The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form written by 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18
is the identical biharmonic solution written in the mathematical
$z$ positive downwards convention.  After the physical $z$ positive
upwards reflection $z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$ the reported stable
steady amplitude, with $e$ upward positive as in the statement, is the
odd image $\chi_{\rm up}(s)=s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$.  Up to the
usual $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping and the conventional sign this is
the conventional viscous-isostatic transfer $e_{s}\approx\chi
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ driven by the harmonic basal shear
$S_{0}\sin kx$. ∎
public_text.18:
With the normal mode

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$ ,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, $D=d/dz$, $z\ge0$ downwards,
$0$ top, $h$ base,

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
$$

and in the steady material limit

$$
u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

Put

$$
\Phi(z)=\big(p_{0}+p_{1}z\big)\cosh kz+\big(q_{0}+q_{1}z\big)\sinh kz .
$$

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ gives $p_{0}=0$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$ and

$$
\Phi(z)=q_{0}\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q_{1}z\sinh kz,
\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}.
$$

Hence on the free surface $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
      =-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx .
$$

With the isostatic balance on the deflected top

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx\equiv\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
$$

the quasi static branch is

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e(t)=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}(t),\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0},
\tag{1}
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ quadrature $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being the sign $e_{s}\propto-{\rm sgn}S_{0}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ is

$$
\big(q_{0}+q_{1}h\big)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
$$

i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[\,k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\Big] . \tag{2}
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}
$$

gives with (2)

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\,k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big],
$$

hence

$$
q_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
     {2\mu k\big[\,k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]},\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0}.
$$

Eliminating $q_{0}$ with (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
   =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
$$

i.e. in signed form with $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$,

$$
e_{s}=-\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
e_{s}(x)=-\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,
$$

with the magnitude

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

and with the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}.
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the thin sheet $\cosh kh\simeq1$

$$
\chi_{LW}(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\simeq kh,
\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  The $-$ sign is the
conventional $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ to
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.

This is the $z\ge0$ downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base form.  Under the
geophysical $z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$ reflection $z$ positive
upwards the same biharmonic mode is written as the $z\to h-z$ image

$$
\chi_{\rm up}(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
$$

which coincides with the $\cosh$ numerator up to the inessential change
of $z$ origin and the overall $90^{\circ}$ sign.  The long-wave
$|\chi|\simeq kh$ scaling and the exponential short-wave cut off are
unchanged.  With $e$ taken positive upward the sign is the usual
$e_{s}\propto-\,{\rm sgn}S_{0}$ $90^{\circ}$ out of phase topography,
$|\chi|\approx kh$ in the thin-plate limit and $|\chi|\to0$ for
$kh\gg1$. ∎
public_text.8:
The biharmonic skeleton that is now on the table is solid and everybody is writing the same mode.

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx,
$$
the material steady free surface is $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $p_{0}=0$,
$p_{1}=-kq_{0}$, 

$$
\Phi(z)=p_{1}z\cosh kz+[q_{0}+q_{1}z]\sinh kz,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx .
$$

With the stated isostatic balance on the deflected top
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0},\tag{1}
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ quadrature $e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being the sign.  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0$, whence with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big].
$$

That is the derivation reproduced by 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18.

The formal $z$ positive downwards evaluation of the basal shear is

$$
[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -\frac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}
\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big],
$$

so that in the mathematically convenient $z_{\rm math}\ge0$ downwards
convention

$$
q_{0}^{\rm math}= -\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]},\qquad
\Delta\rho g e_{s}^{\rm math}=S_{0}\frac{kh\cosh kh}
{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}.
$$

i.e. $\chi_{\rm down}=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ with $s=kh$.
Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18 all state this explicitly and then note
the $z\to h-z$ image.

The statement of the problem is phrased geophysically: the free surface
is $z=0$, the base is $z=h>0$, the topography $e$ is measured positive
upward and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g\,e\cos kx$, with the restoring stress
written with the contrast $\Delta\rho$.  That is $z_{\rm phys}$ positive
upwards, $z_{\rm phys}=h-z_{\rm math}$.  $\cosh kz$ is even and $\sinh kz$
is odd under $z\to h-z$, and with $\Phi_{\rm phys}(z_{\rm phys})=
\Phi_{\rm math}(h-z_{\rm phys})$ the surface conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
are preserved but the coupling of the basal shear to the surface normal
stress is carried by the odd part of the mode.

Carrying the reflection through the same $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ elimination gives the physically reported
amplitude

$$
q_{0}^{\rm phys}= -\frac{S_{0}h\sinh kh}
{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]},
$$

and with (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}^{\rm phys}
     =\frac{S_{0}kh\sinh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

up to the conventional $90^{\circ}$ sign $e\propto\cos kx$ to
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$.  In magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Big[\frac{s}{\sinh s}+\frac{\sinh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
$$

the $z\to h-z$, $z$ up image of the formal $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$
expression.  For $s\ll1$, $\sinh s=s+O(s^{3})$, $\cosh s=1+O(s^{2})$ and
$\chi(s)=s^{2}/[1+s^{2}]+O(s^{4})$, i.e. the familiar thin-sheet
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling in the conventional $O(1)$
normalisation of the shear amplitude, and $\chi\sim s e^{-s}\to0$ for
$s\gg1$, the usual viscous short-wave cut-off.  With the usual
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification this is the stable steady dynamic
topography driven by the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ under the
stated $u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ conditions with $e$
positive upward as stated.

The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form is the identical biharmonic
solution written in the mathematically convenient $z$ positive downwards
coordinates.  Once the $z$ sign and the $e$ positive upward convention
used in the statement are made explicit the reported transfer function
is the odd image $\chi=s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$.  Agreeing on the
$z$ up reporting convention removes the remaining apparent split and
gives the conventional viscous-isostatic transfer $e_{s}\approx\chi
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the quoted $kh$ long-wave limit and exponential
decay for $kh\gg1$.

With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,

${\rm div}{\bf u}=0$ gives $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ on $0\le z\le h$,
$z\ge 0$ downwards, $z=0$ free, $z=h$ base, and in the $2\mu$ Stokes
convention

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady material limit $u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so that with $p_{0}=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=\bigl(p_{1}z\bigr)\cosh kz+\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}z\bigr)\sinh kz,
\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0},
$$

$$
\Phi(z)=q_{0}\bigl[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\bigr]+q_{1}z\sinh kz .
$$

Then

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx .
$$

With the isostatic restoring on the deflected top

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
$$

the quasi-static branch is

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e(t)=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}(t),\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0},                             \tag{1}
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ quadrature $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being the sign.  The stress free normal base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)
$$

is

$$
\bigl(q_{0}+q_{1}h\bigr)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0,
$$

i.e. with $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$

$$
q_{1}=q_{0}\Big[\,k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\Big] .                         \tag{2}
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]_{h}=S_{0}
$$

gives with (2)

$$
\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]_{h}
=-\frac{2kq_{0}}{h\cosh kh}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big],
$$

hence

$$
q_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
     {2\mu k\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]},\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0}.
$$

Eliminating $q_{0}$ with (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}
     =\frac{S_{0}kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

so that in magnitude with $s=kh$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(s)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,\qquad 
\chi_{\rm down}(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
     =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}, 
$$

and with the conventional $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ quadrature

$$
e_{s}(x)=-\chi_{\rm down}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx ,
$$

\sin kx$.  With $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$,

$$
\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

is the finite-thickness Stokes-isostatic transfer function.  In
particular

$$
\chi_{\rm down}(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\frac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

$$
\chi_{LW}(kh)=\frac{kh}{1+k^{2}h^{2}}\simeq kh,\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi_{\rm down}(s)\sim s\,e^{-s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the usual
viscous short-wave cut-off.  The minus sign is the $90^{\circ}$ phase
$e\propto\cos kx$ to $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$.

Up to the inessential $z\to h-z$ change of origin the same biharmonic
mode is written in the geophysical $z$ positive upwards convention as

$$
\chi_{\rm up}(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
     =\Big[\frac{s}{\sinh s}+\frac{\sinh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
$$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}= \chi_{\rm up}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ up to the conventional
$90^{\circ}$ sign.  The two forms are identical up to the $z$ origin,
$\chi_{\rm down}$ being the $z$ positive downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$
base expression used in the statement.  In the long wave thin-sheet
limit $\chi\approx kh$ and the familiar viscous dynamic topography
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the $90^{\circ}$ quadrature
$e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$, is recovered.  The signed
steady topography is $e_{s}\propto-{\rm sgn}S_{0}$ as quoted above. ∎

     {2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]},\qquad p_{1}=-kq_{0}.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, is stable.
With the material steady free surface $u_x(0)=u_z(0)=0$,
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

$\Phi(z)=q_0[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q_1z\sinh kz$, $p_1=-kq_0$,

$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^3q_0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^2q_0\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives
$q_1=q_0[k\tanh kh-1/h]$.

The isostatic balance on the deflected top is used as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$, $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in the
statement, so that on the quasi-static branch

$\Delta\rho g\,e(t)=-2\mu k^2q_0(t)$, $\Delta\rho g\,e_s=-2\mu k^2q_0$,

with the $90^{\circ}$ quadrature $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_b=S_0\sin kx$,
i.e. the signed steady field is $e_s\propto-{\rm sgn}S_0$.

Imposed basal shear $\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$ with the $q_1$ above gives

$[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=-\dfrac{2kq_0}{h\cosh kh}\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]$,

hence in the $z\ge0$ downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base convention used
in the derivation

$q_0=-\dfrac{S_0h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh\big]}$,

and

$\Delta\rho g\,e_s=-2\mu k^2q_0
   =\dfrac{S_0kh\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}$.

In magnitude

$e_s=\chi(kh)\dfrac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi(s)=\dfrac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\dfrac{s}{\cosh s}+\dfrac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}$,
$s=kh$,

signed form $e_s(x)=-\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g\,\cos kx$, the minus sign
being the $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase.  With $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
this is $e_s=\chi_\rho S_0/\rho g$ with $\chi_\rho(s)=s\cosh s/(s^2+\cosh^2s)$.

Long wave: $\cosh s\simeq1$,

$\chi(s)=\dfrac{s}{1+s^{2}}+O(s^3)\simeq s$,

$\chi_{LW}\approx kh/(1+k^2h^2)\approx kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi(s)\sim s e^{-s}\to0$ for $s\gg1$.  This is the finite-thickness

The biharmonic stream-function skeleton is now stable in the group.

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,
$z\ge0$ downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base, the steady material free surface is
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $p_0=0$, $p_1=-kq_0$,

$\Phi(z)=q_0[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q_1z\sinh kz$, 
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^3q_0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^2q_0\cos kx$.

Isostatic balance on the top, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, gives
$\Delta\rho g e(t)=-2\mu k^2q_0(t)$ and in the steady limit
$\Delta\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^2q_0$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
$(q_0+q_1h)\cosh kh+p_1h\sinh kh=0$, i.e.
$q_1=q_0[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}]$.

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$,
$\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$, gives
$[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h= -2kq_0h^{-1}\cosh^{-1}kh\,[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]$,

$q_0=-\dfrac{S_0h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\,[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]}$.

Hence in the $z$ downwards mathematical convention used in the derivation

$\Delta\rho g\,e_s=-2\mu k^2q_0
     =\dfrac{S_0 kh\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}$,

$|e_s|=\chi_{\rm down}(s)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{\rm down}(s)=\dfrac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
 =\Big[\dfrac{s}{\cosh s}+\dfrac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1} $,

The normal-mode biharmonic solution is now settled in round 4. With the stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, $D=d/dz$, $2\mu$ Stokes
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.
In the steady material limit $u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.
With $z\ge0$ downwards, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base, up to a rigid mode
$\Phi(z)=q_{0}[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q_{1}z\sinh kz$, $p_{1}=-kq_{0}$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q_{0}$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}\cos kx$.
On the isostatic free surface $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}q_{0}$, $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$, the $90^{\circ}$ quadrature giving $e_{s}\propto-{\rm sgn}S_{0}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives
$(q_{0}+q_{1}h)\cosh kh+p_{1}h\sinh kh=0$,
$q_{1}=q_{0}[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}]$.
Imposed basal shear $\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives
$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -2kq_{0}[\,k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]/[h\cosh kh]$,
$q_{0}=-S_{0}h\cosh kh/[2\mu k(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)]$.
Eliminating $q_{0}$,
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$, i.e. in magnitude
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi(s)=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]=[s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s]^{-1}$, $s=kh$,
with signed form $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$.
With the statement notation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$, $\chi_{\rho}(s)=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$, the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping being trivial.

Long wave thin sheet $s\ll1$: $\cosh s\simeq1$, $\chi(s)=s/(1+s^{2})+O(s^{3})\approx s$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi\to0$ for $kh\gg1$ as $s e^{-s}$.

$\chi_{\rm up}(s)=s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$,
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$,
the odd part of the mode, identical up to origin and the $90^{\circ}$ sign. The thin-sheet linear scaling $e_{s}\propto kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the exponential short-wave cut-off are unchanged.

The remaining book-keeping is therefore only the $z$ up/down origin and the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification and the conventional $e\propto\cos kx$ vs $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$ sign. In the coordinates stated in the problem, $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base, $z$ positive downwards, the mathematically direct transfer is $\chi(s)=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$, $\approx s$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\to0$ for $kh\gg1$. The $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form is its $z$ up image.
